tasks.summary: Studies how sequence encoders maintain integer counters across in-distribution and length-out-of-distribution inputs.
tasks.description_md:
# Synth-Counting

## Research Question
Can you design a sequence-model architecture that maintains *integer counters*
robustly across in-distribution **and** length-out-of-distribution test inputs?
The component under study is the **encoder architecture** (recurrent /
transformer / state-space / hybrid) — initialization, optimizer, training loop,
loss, evaluation, and data generators are fixed.

## Background
Counting is one of the oldest probes of sequence-model expressivity. Weiss,
Goldberg & Yahav (ACL 2018, arXiv:1805.04908) showed that finite-precision
LSTMs can learn to implement integer counters and extrapolate to inputs longer
than those seen at training time, while Bhattamishra, Ahuja & Goyal
(EMNLP 2020, arXiv:2009.11264) demonstrated that vanilla Transformers with
sinusoidal positional encodings collapse on counter languages such as
a^n b^n c^n when the test length leaves the training range. More recent work —
notably McLeish et al. ("Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right
Embeddings", NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2405.17399, repo
https://github.com/mcleish7/arithmetic) — has shown that with the *right
positional embeddings* (Abacus PE indexing offsets within a contiguous numeric
block) Transformers can extrapolate 6x in length on counting-style tasks.

## Fixed Setup

| Label        | Task                                          | Train length     | OOD length          |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------|------------------|---------------------|
| `exact`      | Regress `y = #(a in x)` over `{a, b}^T`       | `T in [8, 64]`   | `T in [128, 256]` (score = OOD accuracy) |
| `abc`        | Binary classify `a^n b^n c^n` vs corruptions  | `3n in [3, 63]`  | logged on `n in [22, 85]`; score = in-dist accuracy |
| `length-ood` | Same generator as `abc`, but the score is the **retention** `1 - max(0, in_dist_acc - ood_acc)` on `n in (T/3, 4T/3]` | `3n in [3, 63]`  | `n in [22, 85]`     |

Each environment uses the same fixed training loop (6,000 steps of AdamW,
batch 64, smooth-L1 for regression / BCE-with-logits for classification) and
evaluates on 1,024 freshly drawn examples per split. All data is generated on
the fly — no network or filesystem access required.

## What You Can Modify
Edit only the body of `build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module` in
`pytorch-examples/synth_counting/custom_strategy.py` (the EDITABLE block
labelled in the file). The returned module must satisfy:

* **Input**: `tokens` `LongTensor[B, T]` padded with `config.pad_id`; the first
  position is always a CLS token. `lengths` `LongTensor[B]` gives the true
  length **including** the CLS token.
* **Output**: a tensor of shape `[B, config.hidden_dim]` representing the
  pooled sequence summary. The fixed head turns that into a scalar.
* **Capacity**: at most 5,000,000 parameters (asserted at startup).

You may freely change the encoder type (RNN, Transformer, SSM, …), positional
embedding scheme, number of layers, attention pattern, etc. The interface
contract is the only hard constraint.

## Metrics
For every environment the script prints `FINAL_METRICS` and `TEST_METRICS`
lines containing `in_dist_accuracy`, `ood_accuracy`, `extrapolation_gap`, and
the primary `score` (already in `[0, 1]`). The aggregate task score is the
geometric mean across the three environments.

## Baselines

| Baseline      | Architecture                                                                                                                                                          | Notes / Reference                                                                                                       |
|---------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `lstm`        | 2-layer LSTM reading the last hidden state                                                                                                                            | Weiss, Goldberg & Yahav 2018 counter recipe (arXiv:1805.04908).                                                         |
| `transformer` | 2-layer Transformer encoder, 4 heads, sinusoidal PE, CLS pooling                                                                                                      | Bhattamishra et al. 2020 (arXiv:2009.11264).                                                                            |
| `abacus`      | 2-layer Transformer with Abacus-style count-positional embeddings (1-based offset within the current run-length, with random training offsets, added to the token embedding) | McLeish et al. 2024 (arXiv:2405.17399, repo https://github.com/mcleish7/arithmetic).                                     |
tasks.description_html:
Synth-Counting

Research Question

Can you design a sequence-model architecture that maintains integer counters robustly across in-distribution and length-out-of-distribution test inputs? The component under study is the encoder architecture (recurrent / transformer / state-space / hybrid) — initialization, optimizer, training loop, loss, evaluation, and data generators are fixed.

Background

Counting is one of the oldest probes of sequence-model expressivity. Weiss, Goldberg & Yahav (ACL 2018, arXiv:1805.04908) showed that finite-precision LSTMs can learn to implement integer counters and extrapolate to inputs longer than those seen at training time, while Bhattamishra, Ahuja & Goyal (EMNLP 2020, arXiv:2009.11264) demonstrated that vanilla Transformers with sinusoidal positional encodings collapse on counter languages such as a^n b^n c^n when the test length leaves the training range. More recent work — notably McLeish et al. ("Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings", NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2405.17399, repo https://github.com/mcleish7/arithmetic) — has shown that with the right positional embeddings (Abacus PE indexing offsets within a contiguous numeric block) Transformers can extrapolate 6x in length on counting-style tasks.

Fixed Setup

Label Task Train length OOD length
exact Regress y = #(a in x) over {a, b}^T T in [8, 64] T in [128, 256] (score = OOD accuracy)
abc Binary classify a^n b^n c^n vs corruptions 3n in [3, 63] logged on n in [22, 85]; score = in-dist accuracy
length-ood Same generator as abc, but the score is the retention 1 - max(0, in_dist_acc - ood_acc) on n in (T/3, 4T/3] 3n in [3, 63] n in [22, 85]

Each environment uses the same fixed training loop (6,000 steps of AdamW, batch 64, smooth-L1 for regression / BCE-with-logits for classification) and evaluates on 1,024 freshly drawn examples per split. All data is generated on the fly — no network or filesystem access required.

What You Can Modify

Edit only the body of build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module in pytorch-examples/synth_counting/custom_strategy.py (the EDITABLE block labelled in the file). The returned module must satisfy:

  • Input: tokens LongTensor[B, T] padded with config.pad_id; the first position is always a CLS token. lengths LongTensor[B] gives the true length including the CLS token.
  • Output: a tensor of shape [B, config.hidden_dim] representing the pooled sequence summary. The fixed head turns that into a scalar.
  • Capacity: at most 5,000,000 parameters (asserted at startup).

You may freely change the encoder type (RNN, Transformer, SSM, …), positional embedding scheme, number of layers, attention pattern, etc. The interface contract is the only hard constraint.

Metrics

For every environment the script prints FINAL_METRICS and TEST_METRICS lines containing in_dist_accuracy, ood_accuracy, extrapolation_gap, and the primary score (already in [0, 1]). The aggregate task score is the geometric mean across the three environments.

Baselines

Baseline Architecture Notes / Reference
lstm 2-layer LSTM reading the last hidden state Weiss, Goldberg & Yahav 2018 counter recipe (arXiv:1805.04908).
transformer 2-layer Transformer encoder, 4 heads, sinusoidal PE, CLS pooling Bhattamishra et al. 2020 (arXiv:2009.11264).
abacus 2-layer Transformer with Abacus-style count-positional embeddings (1-based offset within the current run-length, with random training offsets, added to the token embedding) McLeish et al. 2024 (arXiv:2405.17399, repo https://github.com/mcleish7/arithmetic).

files.content:
"""Synth-counting scaffold for MLS-Bench.

The benchmark probes whether a sequence model can maintain *integer counters*
that generalize to test sequences much longer than those seen at training time.
Three environments are exercised by the same scaffold:

  * ``exact``    - regress y = #(a in x_{1:T}) on binary sequences over {a, b}.
                   Train length T ~ U[8, 64]; tested on the same range and on
                   2x-4x longer hold-outs (length-OOD).
  * ``abc``      - classify whether the input matches a^n b^n c^n with n drawn
                   in U[1, T_train]; tested on n in U[1, T_train] AND on a held-
                   out 2x-4x-longer range.
  * ``length_ood`` - report the in-distribution vs 4x-OOD accuracy gap for the
                     a^n b^n c^n environment (separate metric, same data
                     generator) so the parser can score length extrapolation.

The model architecture is the only piece the agent edits.  Training loop,
optimizer, evaluation, and metric reporting are fixed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import random
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field, replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch import nn


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Benchmark configuration
# =====================================================================
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskConfig:
    env: str = "exact"
    vocab_size: int = 5  # 0=PAD, 1=a, 2=b, 3=c, 4=BOS/CLS
    pad_id: int = 0
    a_id: int = 1
    b_id: int = 2
    c_id: int = 3
    cls_id: int = 4
    train_max_len: int = 64
    ood_multiplier: int = 4
    train_steps: int = 6_000
    eval_examples: int = 1_024
    batch_size: int = 64
    log_interval: int = 1000
    hidden_dim: int = 128


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunResult:
    in_dist_metric: float
    ood_metric: float
    extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


DEFAULT_TASK = TaskConfig()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Synthetic data generators (all on the fly; no network, no files)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
def _pad_batch(seqs: list[list[int]], pad_id: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    max_len = max(len(s) for s in seqs)
    out = torch.full((len(seqs), max_len), pad_id, dtype=torch.long)
    for i, s in enumerate(seqs):
        out[i, : len(s)] = torch.tensor(s, dtype=torch.long)
    return out


def make_exact_batch(
    config: TaskConfig, batch_size: int, length_range: tuple[int, int], rng: random.Random
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Return (tokens, lengths, count_target) for the exact-count environment."""
    lo, hi = length_range
    seqs: list[list[int]] = []
    targets: list[int] = []
    for _ in range(batch_size):
        T = rng.randint(lo, hi)
        seq = [rng.choice([config.a_id, config.b_id]) for _ in range(T)]
        seqs.append([config.cls_id] + seq)
        targets.append(sum(1 for t in seq if t == config.a_id))
    tokens = _pad_batch(seqs, config.pad_id)
    lengths = torch.tensor([len(s) for s in seqs], dtype=torch.long)
    counts = torch.tensor(targets, dtype=torch.float32)
    return tokens, lengths, counts


def make_abc_batch(
    config: TaskConfig, batch_size: int, n_range: tuple[int, int], rng: random.Random
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Return (tokens, lengths, label) for the a^n b^n c^n membership task.

    Half of the batch are positive (matching a^n b^n c^n); the other half are
    structured negatives drawn from corruptions: wrong block counts, wrong
    order, or swapped middle symbols.  Both classes share the same length
    distribution so length alone is not a signal.
    """
    lo, hi = n_range
    seqs: list[list[int]] = []
    labels: list[int] = []
    for i in range(batch_size):
        n = rng.randint(lo, hi)
        if i % 2 == 0:
            seq = [config.a_id] * n + [config.b_id] * n + [config.c_id] * n
            label = 1
        else:
            kind = rng.randrange(4)
            if kind == 0:  # wrong b count: a^n b^(n+d) c^n
                d = rng.choice([-2, -1, 1, 2])
                nb = max(1, n + d)
                seq = [config.a_id] * n + [config.b_id] * nb + [config.c_id] * n
            elif kind == 1:  # wrong c count: a^n b^n c^(n+d)
                d = rng.choice([-2, -1, 1, 2])
                nc = max(1, n + d)
                seq = [config.a_id] * n + [config.b_id] * n + [config.c_id] * nc
            elif kind == 2:  # wrong order: shuffle one element between blocks
                seq = [config.a_id] * n + [config.b_id] * n + [config.c_id] * n
                if n >= 1:
                    i1 = rng.randrange(n)
                    i2 = rng.randrange(n, 2 * n)
                    seq[i1], seq[i2] = seq[i2], seq[i1]
            else:  # interleave a/b in middle
                seq = [config.a_id] * n + [config.b_id] * n + [config.c_id] * n
                if 2 * n >= 2:
                    swap = rng.randrange(n - 1) if n >= 2 else 0
                    seq[swap], seq[swap + n] = seq[swap + n], seq[swap]
            label = 0
        seqs.append([config.cls_id] + seq)
        labels.append(label)
    tokens = _pad_batch(seqs, config.pad_id)
    lengths = torch.tensor([len(s) for s in seqs], dtype=torch.long)
    labels_t = torch.tensor(labels, dtype=torch.float32)
    return tokens, lengths, labels_t


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared training/evaluation utilities (FIXED)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
def set_global_seed(seed: int) -> None:
    random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


def to_device(batch: Iterable[torch.Tensor], device: torch.device) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
    return [b.to(device) if isinstance(b, torch.Tensor) else b for b in batch]


def make_head(env: str, hidden_dim: int) -> nn.Module:
    """One linear head: regression for exact, binary classifier for abc."""
    return nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 1)


# =====================================================================
# EDITABLE: build_model returns a sequence encoder
# =====================================================================
# Interface contract (do not change):
#   build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module
#     The returned module must accept (tokens, lengths) where:
#       * tokens: LongTensor[B, T], padded with config.pad_id, position 0 is
#                 always config.cls_id.
#       * lengths: LongTensor[B] true sequence length INCLUDING the CLS token.
#     and must return a tensor of shape [B, config.hidden_dim] giving the
#     CLS-position representation that the FIXED head consumes.
#
# You may freely change the architecture (RNN / Transformer / SSM / hybrid),
# positional encodings, layer counts, etc., but the input/output shapes must
# match the contract above and parameter count should stay <= 5M for fairness.
# =====================================================================
def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Default scaffold: a 2-layer GRU encoder reading the final hidden state.

    Note: the prepended CLS token is at position 0, BEFORE any content token,
    so a causal/left-to-right encoder must read the *last* valid position to
    summarise the sequence.  Bidirectional or self-attention models may pool
    over the CLS position instead.
    """

    class GRUEncoder(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, cfg: TaskConfig):
            super().__init__()
            self.embed = nn.Embedding(cfg.vocab_size, cfg.hidden_dim, padding_idx=cfg.pad_id)
            self.rnn = nn.GRU(
                input_size=cfg.hidden_dim,
                hidden_size=cfg.hidden_dim,
                num_layers=2,
                batch_first=True,
            )
            self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(cfg.hidden_dim)

        def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor, lengths: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            h = self.embed(tokens)
            out, _ = self.rnn(h)
            last_idx = (lengths - 1).clamp(min=0).view(-1, 1, 1).expand(-1, 1, out.size(-1))
            last = out.gather(1, last_idx).squeeze(1)
            return self.norm(last)

    return GRUEncoder(config)


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: training and evaluation driver
# =====================================================================
class SequenceModel(nn.Module):
    """Wrap the agent-built encoder with the fixed task head."""

    def __init__(self, config: TaskConfig):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        self.encoder = build_model(config)
        self.head = make_head(config.env, config.hidden_dim)

    def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor, lengths: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        feats = self.encoder(tokens, lengths)
        if feats.dim() != 2 or feats.shape[1] != self.config.hidden_dim:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Encoder must return shape [B, {self.config.hidden_dim}], got {tuple(feats.shape)}"
            )
        return self.head(feats).squeeze(-1)


def compute_loss(env: str, preds: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    if env == "exact":
        # Smooth-L1 regression toward the (normalised) count.
        return F.smooth_l1_loss(preds, targets)
    return F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(preds, targets)


def metric_value(env: str, preds: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    if env == "exact":
        # Accuracy under "rounded prediction equals target".
        return (preds.round() == targets).float().mean().item()
    return (((preds > 0).float()) == targets).float().mean().item()


def _make_batch(env: str, config: TaskConfig, batch_size: int, length_range: tuple[int, int], rng: random.Random):
    if env == "exact":
        return make_exact_batch(config, batch_size, length_range, rng)
    return make_abc_batch(config, batch_size, length_range, rng)


def evaluate(
    model: nn.Module,
    config: TaskConfig,
    length_range: tuple[int, int],
    n_examples: int,
    device: torch.device,
    rng: random.Random,
) -> float:
    model.eval()
    seen = 0
    metric_sum = 0.0
    weight = 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        while seen < n_examples:
            bs = min(config.batch_size, n_examples - seen)
            tokens, lengths, targets = _make_batch(config.env, config, bs, length_range, rng)
            tokens, lengths, targets = to_device([tokens, lengths, targets], device)
            preds = model(tokens, lengths)
            metric_sum += metric_value(config.env, preds, targets) * bs
            weight += bs
            seen += bs
    model.train()
    return metric_sum / max(weight, 1)


def train_and_evaluate(config: TaskConfig, seed: int, device: torch.device) -> RunResult:
    set_global_seed(seed)
    model = SequenceModel(config).to(device)
    n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
    if n_params > 5_000_000:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Model has {n_params} > 5M parameters; please reduce capacity.")
    print(f"MODEL_INFO params={n_params}", flush=True)

    optim = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=3e-4, weight_decay=1e-2)

    train_rng = random.Random(seed + 1)
    in_eval_rng = random.Random(seed + 2)
    ood_eval_rng = random.Random(seed + 3)

    if config.env == "exact":
        train_range = (8, config.train_max_len)
        in_dist_range = train_range
        ood_range = (config.train_max_len * 2, config.train_max_len * config.ood_multiplier)
    else:
        train_range = (1, config.train_max_len // 3)  # 3n <= train_max_len
        in_dist_range = train_range
        ood_max_n = (config.train_max_len * config.ood_multiplier) // 3
        ood_range = (config.train_max_len // 3 + 1, ood_max_n)

    print(
        f"TASK_CONFIG env={config.env} train_range={train_range} ood_range={ood_range} "
        f"train_steps={config.train_steps} hidden_dim={config.hidden_dim}",
        flush=True,
    )

    model.train()
    start = time.time()
    running_loss = 0.0
    running_acc = 0.0
    running_n = 0
    for step in range(1, config.train_steps + 1):
        tokens, lengths, targets = _make_batch(config.env, config, config.batch_size, train_range, train_rng)
        tokens, lengths, targets = to_device([tokens, lengths, targets], device)
        preds = model(tokens, lengths)
        loss = compute_loss(config.env, preds, targets)
        optim.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss.backward()
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)
        optim.step()

        running_loss += loss.item()
        running_acc += metric_value(config.env, preds.detach(), targets)
        running_n += 1
        if step == 1 or step % config.log_interval == 0 or step == config.train_steps:
            print(
                f"TRAIN_METRICS env={config.env} step={step} "
                f"loss={running_loss / running_n:.6f} train_metric={running_acc / running_n:.4f}",
                flush=True,
            )
            running_loss = 0.0
            running_acc = 0.0
            running_n = 0

    elapsed = time.time() - start
    in_dist_metric = evaluate(model, config, in_dist_range, config.eval_examples, device, in_eval_rng)
    ood_metric = evaluate(model, config, ood_range, config.eval_examples, device, ood_eval_rng)
    extra = {"train_seconds": elapsed, "train_range": list(train_range), "ood_range": list(ood_range)}
    return RunResult(in_dist_metric=in_dist_metric, ood_metric=ood_metric, extra=extra)


def resolve_device(device_arg: str) -> torch.device:
    if device_arg == "cpu":
        return torch.device("cpu")
    if device_arg == "cuda":
        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
            raise RuntimeError("CUDA requested but not available.")
        return torch.device("cuda")
    return torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="MLS-Bench synth-counting task.")
    parser.add_argument("--env", choices=("exact", "abc", "length_ood"), default="exact")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--label", type=str, default="eval")
    parser.add_argument("--device", choices=("auto", "cpu", "cuda"), default="auto")
    parser.add_argument("--train-max-len", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--ood-multiplier", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--train-steps", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--hidden-dim", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="Shrink for quick local check.")
    return parser.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    cfg = DEFAULT_TASK
    # length_ood reuses the abc data generator under the hood and reports the
    # gap as its primary score so a single label cleanly maps to a single env.
    underlying_env = "abc" if args.env == "length_ood" else args.env
    cfg = replace(cfg, env=underlying_env)
    if args.train_max_len is not None:
        cfg = replace(cfg, train_max_len=args.train_max_len)
    if args.ood_multiplier is not None:
        cfg = replace(cfg, ood_multiplier=args.ood_multiplier)
    if args.train_steps is not None:
        cfg = replace(cfg, train_steps=args.train_steps)
    if args.hidden_dim is not None:
        cfg = replace(cfg, hidden_dim=args.hidden_dim)
    if args.smoke:
        cfg = replace(cfg, train_steps=400, eval_examples=128, log_interval=500, train_max_len=32)

    device = resolve_device(args.device)
    result = train_and_evaluate(cfg, args.seed, device)

    if args.env == "exact":
        primary = result.in_dist_metric
        gap = max(0.0, result.in_dist_metric - result.ood_metric)
        metrics = {
            "in_dist_accuracy": result.in_dist_metric,
            "ood_accuracy": result.ood_metric,
            "extrapolation_gap": gap,
            "score": result.ood_metric,
        }
    elif args.env == "abc":
        metrics = {
            "in_dist_accuracy": result.in_dist_metric,
            "ood_accuracy": result.ood_metric,
            "extrapolation_gap": max(0.0, result.in_dist_metric - result.ood_metric),
            "score": result.in_dist_metric,
        }
    else:  # length_ood
        # Reward retention of accuracy from in-dist to OOD: clamp negative gaps.
        gap = max(0.0, result.in_dist_metric - result.ood_metric)
        retention = 1.0 - gap  # in [0, 1] when in_dist >= ood
        metrics = {
            "in_dist_accuracy": result.in_dist_metric,
            "ood_accuracy": result.ood_metric,
            "extrapolation_gap": gap,
            "retention": retention,
            "score": retention,
        }

    summary = {
        "env": args.env,
        "config": asdict(cfg),
        "metrics": metrics,
        "extra": result.extra,
    }
    final_str = " ".join(f"{k}={v:.6f}" if isinstance(v, float) else f"{k}={v}" for k, v in metrics.items())
    print(f"FINAL_METRICS {final_str}", flush=True)
    print(f"TEST_METRICS {final_str}", flush=True)

    if args.output_dir is not None:
        args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out = args.output_dir / f"{args.label}_seed{args.seed}.json"
        out.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

transformer.content:
def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Vanilla Transformer encoder with sinusoidal positional encodings."""

    class SinusoidalPE(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, dim: int, max_len: int = 4096):
            super().__init__()
            pe = torch.zeros(max_len, dim)
            position = torch.arange(0, max_len, dtype=torch.float).unsqueeze(1)
            div_term = torch.exp(torch.arange(0, dim, 2).float() * -(math.log(10000.0) / dim))
            pe[:, 0::2] = torch.sin(position * div_term)
            pe[:, 1::2] = torch.cos(position * div_term)
            self.register_buffer("pe", pe.unsqueeze(0))

        def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            T = x.size(1)
            if T > self.pe.size(1):
                # Extend on the fly so OOD lengths do not crash; values past
                # max_len fall back to zero (still part of the standard recipe).
                extra = torch.zeros(1, T - self.pe.size(1), x.size(-1), device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
                pe = torch.cat([self.pe.to(x.dtype), extra], dim=1)
            else:
                pe = self.pe[:, :T].to(x.dtype)
            return x + pe

    class TransformerEncoder(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, cfg: TaskConfig):
            super().__init__()
            self.cfg = cfg
            self.embed = nn.Embedding(cfg.vocab_size, cfg.hidden_dim, padding_idx=cfg.pad_id)
            self.pe = SinusoidalPE(cfg.hidden_dim)
            layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
                d_model=cfg.hidden_dim,
                nhead=4,
                dim_feedforward=4 * cfg.hidden_dim,
                dropout=0.0,
                activation="gelu",
                batch_first=True,
                norm_first=True,
            )
            self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(layer, num_layers=2)
            self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(cfg.hidden_dim)

        def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor, lengths: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            x = self.embed(tokens) * math.sqrt(self.cfg.hidden_dim)
            x = self.pe(x)
            key_padding = tokens.eq(self.cfg.pad_id)
            h = self.encoder(x, src_key_padding_mask=key_padding)
            cls = h[:, 0]
            return self.norm(cls)

    return TransformerEncoder(config)

def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Transformer with Abacus-style count-positional embeddings (McLeish 2024)."""

    class AbacusPE(nn.Module):
        def __init__(
            self,
            dim: int,
            max_count: int = 4096,
            pad_id: int = 0,
            cls_id: int = 4,
            train_offset: int = 100,
        ):
            super().__init__()
            self.pad_id = pad_id
            self.cls_id = cls_id
            self.max_count = max_count
            self.train_offset = train_offset
            self.embed = nn.Embedding(max_count + 1, dim)
            nn.init.normal_(self.embed.weight, mean=0.0, std=0.02)

        def block_offsets(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            B, T = tokens.shape
            if T == 0:
                return torch.zeros_like(tokens)

            valid = tokens.ne(self.pad_id) & tokens.ne(self.cls_id)
            cur = torch.zeros(B, dtype=torch.long, device=tokens.device)
            prev_token = tokens.new_full((B,), -1)
            prev_valid = torch.zeros(B, dtype=torch.bool, device=tokens.device)
            cols = []
            for t in range(T):
                tok = tokens[:, t]
                is_valid = valid[:, t]
                same_run = is_valid & prev_valid & tok.eq(prev_token)
                cur = torch.where(
                    is_valid,
                    torch.where(same_run, cur + 1, torch.ones_like(cur)),
                    torch.zeros_like(cur),
                )
                cols.append(cur)
                prev_token = tok
                prev_valid = is_valid

            offsets = torch.stack(cols, dim=1).clamp(max=self.max_count)
            if self.training and self.train_offset > 0:
                shift = torch.randint(
                    0,
                    self.train_offset + 1,
                    (),
                    dtype=offsets.dtype,
                    device=offsets.device,
                )
                shifted = (offsets + shift).clamp(max=self.max_count)
                offsets = torch.where(offsets > 0, shifted, offsets)
            return offsets

        def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            offsets = self.block_offsets(tokens)
            return self.embed(offsets)

    class AbacusTransformer(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, cfg: TaskConfig):
            super().__init__()
            self.cfg = cfg
            self.tok_embed = nn.Embedding(cfg.vocab_size, cfg.hidden_dim, padding_idx=cfg.pad_id)
            self.abacus = AbacusPE(cfg.hidden_dim, max_count=4096, pad_id=cfg.pad_id, cls_id=cfg.cls_id)
            layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
                d_model=cfg.hidden_dim,
                nhead=4,
                dim_feedforward=4 * cfg.hidden_dim,
                dropout=0.0,
                activation="gelu",
                batch_first=True,
                norm_first=True,
            )
            self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(layer, num_layers=2)
            self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(cfg.hidden_dim)

        def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor, lengths: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            x = self.tok_embed(tokens) * math.sqrt(self.cfg.hidden_dim)
            x = x + self.abacus(tokens)
            key_padding = tokens.eq(self.cfg.pad_id)
            h = self.encoder(x, src_key_padding_mask=key_padding)
            cls = h[:, 0]
            return self.norm(cls)

    return AbacusTransformer(config)

tasks.description_md:
# Synth-DNF

## Research Question
What differentiable neural architecture and training recipe should you choose to learn
**DNF concepts** (disjunctive normal form Boolean functions) from random
uniform examples?

Formally, a DNF over `n` Boolean variables `x ∈ {0,1}^n` is a function
`f(x) = T_1(x) ∨ T_2(x) ∨ ... ∨ T_s(x)`, where each term `T_l` is a
conjunction (AND) of literals `x_i` or `¬x_i`. The agent is given
uniformly drawn training pairs `(x, f(x))` from a *hidden* random target
DNF and must train a classifier that predicts `f` on a fresh test sample.

## Background
DNF learnability under the uniform distribution is one of the most
studied problems in computational learning theory.

* **Quasi-polynomial bound (Verbeurgt 1990):** any `s`-term DNF can be
  learned in `n^{O(log s/ε)}` time under the uniform distribution from
  random examples — but the dependence on `s` is super-polynomial.
* **Membership-query algorithm (Jackson 1997, Harmonic Sieve):** polynomial
  time, but **requires membership queries** so it is not a "neural
  learner from random samples" baseline.
* **Random-DNF average case (Jackson & Servedio, 2005):** polynomial-time
  algorithms exist for random monotone DNF with `s = O(n^{2-γ})` terms
  and random non-monotone DNF with `s = O(n^{3/2-γ})` terms,
  http://www.cs.columbia.edu/~rocco/papers/random05.html.

On the empirical side, vanilla MLPs and gradient-boosted trees are the
canonical practical baselines on Boolean tabular data; recent
"differentiable DNF" architectures (Payani & Fekri 2019, Mat_DNF 2023)
encode the DNF inductive bias directly into the network.

This task asks: *with random examples only, can you design a differentiable
neural learner that closes (or beats) the gap to GBDTs on the three DNF
regimes below*?

## What You Can Modify
Edit only the EDITABLE region (build_model / make_dataset /
fit_and_predict) of
`pytorch-examples/synth_dnf/custom_strategy.py`. Everything else,
including DNF sampling, test-set construction, and final scoring, is
fixed.

This is a neural-learner ML-science task, not a SAT solver or
membership-query algorithm task. Treat the target DNF as a hidden label
oracle for uniformly sampled examples only; do not inspect or reconstruct
the term list directly.

The three signatures you control:

1. `build_model(config, seed) -> (model, info)` returns an opaque model
   object consumed only by your own `fit_and_predict`.
2. `make_dataset(dnf, config, seed) -> (x, y)` constructs the training
   set. Must use only the API exposed via `evaluate_dnf` /
   `make_uniform_examples`, return inputs in `{0,1}^n` and labels in
   `{0,1}`, and stay within `4 * config.train_size` examples.
3. `fit_and_predict(model, info, train_x, train_y, test_x, config, seed)
   -> predictions` does the actual training and returns an integer 0/1
   prediction vector of length `test_x.shape[0]`.

Available imports include `numpy`, `torch`, standard `sklearn` baselines,
and the helpers `evaluate_dnf`, `make_uniform_examples`.

## Fixed Setup
Three families of random DNF targets are evaluated independently and
combined via geometric mean:

| label                    | n  | s  | w | family               |
|--------------------------|----|----|---|----------------------|
| `random-n30-s10-w4`      | 30 | 10 | 4 | mixed-polarity DNF   |
| `monotone-n40-s20-w4`    | 40 | 20 | 4 | monotone DNF         |
| `sparse-n60-s10-w4`      | 60 | 10 | 4 | 12-variable junta    |

For each environment in the release configuration, one hidden target DNF
is sampled per top-level seed. The learner is fit on one fresh training
set and evaluated on a 10k held-out uniform sample. The reported
`test_accuracy` is that run's held-out accuracy.

## Metric
The leaderboard metric is `test_accuracy` (also emitted as `score`) per
environment, then aggregated by geometric mean across environments.

## Baselines
* **mlp** — 2-hidden-layer ReLU MLP (256, 256) trained with AdamW + BCE
  (the canonical neural baseline; vanilla feed-forward networks have no
  DNF-specific inductive bias).
* **rf** — sklearn `RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200)`, the
  classical bagging-of-trees baseline (Breiman, 2001).
* **gbdt** — sklearn `GradientBoostingClassifier`, a gradient-boosted
  decision-tree baseline for tabular Boolean data (Shwartz-Ziv & Armon,
  arXiv:2106.03253).
* **deep_dnf** — A differentiable DNF architecture with `2s` soft
  conjunctions and a noisy-OR aggregator, trained with literal-sparsity
  regularisation. Follows the "differentiable DNF" family (Payani &
  Fekri 2019, arXiv:1904.01554; Mat_DNF, Machine Learning 2023).

files.content:
"""Synth-DNF scaffold for MLS-Bench.

Research question: how should you design a differentiable neural learner for
DNF concepts under the uniform distribution from random examples?

The fixed evaluation samples a hidden DNF formula and asks the agent to
control only:
  1. The model class (`build_model`)
  2. The training-data construction (`make_dataset`)
  3. The training/fitting routine (`fit_and_predict`)

The benchmark generates a hidden DNF, draws random uniform Boolean examples,
trains the agent-defined learner, and evaluates 0-1 test accuracy on a held-out
uniform sample. Each task variant fixes the DNF family (random / monotone /
sparse) and the (n_features, num_terms, term_width).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import random
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable

import numpy as np


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Benchmark configuration
# =====================================================================
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskConfig:
    """Fixed benchmark configuration.

    n_features        Number of Boolean variables n.
    num_terms         Number of conjunctive terms s in the target DNF.
    term_width        Width w (literals per term) of every term.
    monotone          If True, the DNF contains only positive literals.
    sparse_subset     If > 0, all literals are drawn from a fixed subset
                      of this many variables (sparse / juntas case).
    train_size        Number of training examples (uniform Boolean).
    test_size         Number of held-out test examples.
    num_targets       Number of distinct random DNF concepts per top-level seed.
    num_trainsets     Number of fresh training sets per concept.
    time_budget_sec   Soft wall-clock budget per (target, trainset) run.
    """

    n_features: int = 30
    num_terms: int = 10
    term_width: int = 4
    monotone: bool = False
    sparse_subset: int = 0
    train_size: int = 20_000
    test_size: int = 10_000
    num_targets: int = 1
    num_trainsets: int = 1
    time_budget_sec: float = 90.0


DEFAULT_TASK = TaskConfig()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunResult:
    target_index: int
    trainset_index: int
    fit_seconds: float
    test_accuracy: float


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: DNF sampling and labeling
# =====================================================================
def _sample_term(
    rng: random.Random,
    config: TaskConfig,
    active_variables: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]:
    """Sample a single term as a tuple of (variable_index, polarity) pairs.

    polarity=1 means literal x_i, polarity=0 means literal NOT x_i.
    """
    if config.sparse_subset > 0:
        if active_variables is None or len(active_variables) < config.term_width:
            raise ValueError(
                "sparse DNF sampling requires a fixed active variable set "
                f"with at least term_width={config.term_width} variables."
            )
        variables = rng.sample(list(active_variables), config.term_width)
    else:
        variables = rng.sample(range(config.n_features), config.term_width)
    if config.monotone:
        polarities = [1] * config.term_width
    else:
        polarities = [rng.randint(0, 1) for _ in variables]
    term = tuple(sorted((int(v), int(p)) for v, p in zip(variables, polarities)))
    return term


def sample_dnf(config: TaskConfig, seed: int) -> tuple[tuple[tuple[int, int], ...], ...]:
    """Sample a DNF formula with ``num_terms`` distinct terms."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    active_variables: tuple[int, ...] | None = None
    if config.sparse_subset > 0:
        if config.sparse_subset < config.term_width:
            raise ValueError(
                f"sparse_subset={config.sparse_subset} must be >= term_width={config.term_width}."
            )
        active_variables = tuple(sorted(rng.sample(range(config.n_features), config.sparse_subset)))
    seen: set[tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]] = set()
    terms: list[tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]] = []
    guard = 0
    while len(terms) < config.num_terms:
        guard += 1
        if guard > 10_000 * config.num_terms:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Could not sample enough distinct DNF terms; the configuration "
                "may not admit num_terms distinct terms."
            )
        term = _sample_term(rng, config, active_variables)
        if term in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(term)
        terms.append(term)
    return tuple(terms)


def evaluate_dnf(
    x: np.ndarray,
    dnf: tuple[tuple[tuple[int, int], ...], ...],
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Evaluate the DNF on a batch of Boolean inputs.

    x : array of shape [N, n_features] with values in {0, 1}.
    Returns y of shape [N] with values in {0, 1}.
    """
    y = np.zeros(x.shape[0], dtype=np.int64)
    for term in dnf:
        ok = np.ones(x.shape[0], dtype=bool)
        for var, pol in term:
            if pol == 1:
                ok &= x[:, var] == 1
            else:
                ok &= x[:, var] == 0
        y |= ok.astype(np.int64)
    return y


def make_uniform_examples(
    config: TaskConfig,
    num_examples: int,
    seed: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample uniform random Boolean examples in {0, 1}^n."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    return rng.integers(0, 2, size=(num_examples, config.n_features), dtype=np.int64)


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: dataset/output validation
# =====================================================================
def _validate_dataset(
    dataset: object,
    config: TaskConfig,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    if isinstance(dataset, dict):
        if "x" not in dataset or "y" not in dataset:
            raise ValueError("Dataset dict must contain keys 'x' and 'y'.")
        x, y = dataset["x"], dataset["y"]
    elif isinstance(dataset, (tuple, list)) and len(dataset) == 2:
        x, y = dataset
    else:
        raise TypeError(
            "Dataset must be (x, y) pair or dict with keys 'x' and 'y'."
        )
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.int64)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.int64).reshape(-1)
    if x.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError(f"x must have shape [N, n_features], got {x.shape}.")
    if x.shape[1] != config.n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"x.shape[1] must equal n_features={config.n_features}, got {x.shape[1]}."
        )
    if x.shape[0] == 0:
        raise ValueError("Training dataset must contain at least one example.")
    if x.shape[0] > 4 * config.train_size:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Training dataset size {x.shape[0]} exceeds 4x train_size budget."
        )
    if not np.all((x == 0) | (x == 1)):
        raise ValueError("Training inputs must be in {0, 1}.")
    if not np.all((y == 0) | (y == 1)):
        raise ValueError("Training labels must be in {0, 1}.")
    if x.shape[0] != y.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("x and y must have matching first dimension.")
    return np.ascontiguousarray(x), np.ascontiguousarray(y)


def _validate_predictions(predictions: object, n_test: int) -> np.ndarray:
    preds = np.asarray(predictions).reshape(-1)
    if preds.shape[0] != n_test:
        raise ValueError(
            f"fit_and_predict must return {n_test} predictions, got {preds.shape[0]}."
        )
    preds_int = (preds >= 0.5).astype(np.int64)
    if not np.all((preds_int == 0) | (preds_int == 1)):
        raise ValueError("Predictions must be coercible to {0, 1}.")
    return preds_int


# =====================================================================
# EDITABLE: build_model, make_dataset, fit_and_predict
# =====================================================================
def build_model(config: TaskConfig, seed: int):
    """Return a (model, info) tuple. ``model`` is opaque to the framework
    and only consumed by ``fit_and_predict``. The default is a small MLP.
    """
    import torch
    from torch import nn

    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    hidden = 256
    model = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(config.n_features, hidden),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(hidden, hidden),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(hidden, 1),
    )
    return model, {"kind": "mlp", "hidden": hidden}


def make_dataset(
    dnf: tuple[tuple[tuple[int, int], ...], ...],
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Return a reproducible labeled training set for one target DNF.

    May *not* peek at the held-out test set. The returned dataset is
    validated to have inputs in {0, 1}^n and labels in {0, 1}.
    """
    x = make_uniform_examples(config, config.train_size, seed)
    y = evaluate_dnf(x, dnf)
    return x, y


def fit_and_predict(
    model,
    info: dict,
    train_x: np.ndarray,
    train_y: np.ndarray,
    test_x: np.ndarray,
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Fit ``model`` on (train_x, train_y) and return predictions on test_x.

    Returns a 1-D array of length len(test_x) with values in {0, 1}.
    The default trains an MLP with AdamW and binary cross-entropy.
    """
    import torch
    from torch import nn

    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    model = model.to(device)
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)
    criterion = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()

    train_x_t = torch.from_numpy(train_x).float().to(device)
    train_y_t = torch.from_numpy(train_y).float().to(device)
    test_x_t = torch.from_numpy(test_x).float().to(device)

    epochs = 20
    batch_size = 256
    n = train_x_t.shape[0]
    model.train()
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        perm = torch.randperm(n, device=device)
        for start in range(0, n, batch_size):
            idx = perm[start : start + batch_size]
            logits = model(train_x_t[idx]).view(-1)
            loss = criterion(logits, train_y_t[idx])
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
        if (epoch + 1) % 5 == 0 or epoch == 0:
            with torch.no_grad():
                tr_acc = (
                    ((torch.sigmoid(model(train_x_t)).view(-1) >= 0.5).long()
                     == train_y_t.long()).float().mean().item()
                )
            print(
                f"TRAIN_METRICS epoch={epoch + 1} loss={loss.item():.4f} train_acc={tr_acc:.4f}",
                flush=True,
            )
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        preds = (torch.sigmoid(model(test_x_t)).view(-1) >= 0.5).long().cpu().numpy()
    return preds


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: training driver
# =====================================================================
def run_one(
    target_index: int,
    trainset_index: int,
    dnf: tuple[tuple[tuple[int, int], ...], ...],
    config: TaskConfig,
    train_seed: int,
    fit_seed: int,
    test_x: np.ndarray,
    test_y: np.ndarray,
) -> RunResult:
    import time

    train_x, train_y = _validate_dataset(make_dataset(dnf, config, train_seed), config)
    model, info = build_model(config, fit_seed)
    pos_rate = float(train_y.mean())
    print(
        "DATASET_METRICS "
        f"target={target_index} trainset={trainset_index} "
        f"num_train={train_x.shape[0]} positive_rate={pos_rate:.4f}",
        flush=True,
    )
    start = time.time()
    preds = fit_and_predict(model, info if isinstance(info, dict) else {}, train_x, train_y, test_x, config, fit_seed)
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    preds = _validate_predictions(preds, test_x.shape[0])
    acc = float((preds == test_y).mean())
    print(
        "RUN_METRICS "
        f"target={target_index} trainset={trainset_index} "
        f"fit_seconds={elapsed:.2f} test_accuracy={acc:.6f}",
        flush=True,
    )
    return RunResult(
        target_index=target_index,
        trainset_index=trainset_index,
        fit_seconds=elapsed,
        test_accuracy=acc,
    )


def maybe_apply_smoke_mode(config: TaskConfig, enabled: bool) -> TaskConfig:
    if not enabled:
        return config
    return replace(
        config,
        train_size=2_000,
        test_size=1_000,
        num_targets=1,
        num_trainsets=1,
        time_budget_sec=30.0,
    )


def run_benchmark(config: TaskConfig, seed: int) -> dict[str, object]:
    print(
        "TASK_CONFIG "
        + " ".join(
            [
                f"n={config.n_features}",
                f"s={config.num_terms}",
                f"w={config.term_width}",
                f"monotone={int(config.monotone)}",
                f"sparse_subset={config.sparse_subset}",
                f"train_size={config.train_size}",
                f"test_size={config.test_size}",
                f"num_targets={config.num_targets}",
                f"num_trainsets={config.num_trainsets}",
            ]
        ),
        flush=True,
    )
    results: list[RunResult] = []
    base_seed = int(seed)
    for target_index in range(config.num_targets):
        dnf_seed = base_seed * 10_000 + target_index * 7
        dnf = sample_dnf(config, dnf_seed)
        positive_terms = sum(1 for term in dnf for _, p in term if p == 1)
        print(
            "DNF_SAMPLE "
            f"target={target_index} num_terms={len(dnf)} "
            f"positive_literal_count={positive_terms}",
            flush=True,
        )
        test_seed = base_seed * 20_000 + target_index * 11
        test_x = make_uniform_examples(config, config.test_size, test_seed)
        test_y = evaluate_dnf(test_x, dnf)
        for trainset_index in range(config.num_trainsets):
            train_seed = base_seed * 30_000 + target_index * 1_000 + trainset_index
            fit_seed = base_seed * 40_000 + target_index * 1_000 + trainset_index
            results.append(
                run_one(
                    target_index=target_index,
                    trainset_index=trainset_index,
                    dnf=dnf,
                    config=config,
                    train_seed=train_seed,
                    fit_seed=fit_seed,
                    test_x=test_x,
                    test_y=test_y,
                )
            )

    acc = np.array([r.test_accuracy for r in results], dtype=np.float64)
    fit_t = np.array([r.fit_seconds for r in results], dtype=np.float64)
    base_rate = max(float(np.mean([float((evaluate_dnf(make_uniform_examples(config, 4096, base_seed * 50000 + i), sample_dnf(config, base_seed * 10_000 + i * 7)).mean())) for i in range(min(3, config.num_targets))])), 1e-6)
    final_metrics = {
        "test_accuracy": float(acc.mean()),
        "score": float(acc.mean()),
        "test_accuracy_std": float(acc.std(ddof=0)),
        "mean_fit_seconds": float(fit_t.mean()),
        "base_rate_majority": float(max(base_rate, 1 - base_rate)),
        "num_runs": int(len(results)),
    }
    print(
        "FINAL_METRICS "
        + " ".join(
            f"{k}={v:.6f}" if isinstance(v, float) else f"{k}={v}"
            for k, v in final_metrics.items()
        ),
        flush=True,
    )
    print(
        f"TEST_METRICS test_accuracy={final_metrics['test_accuracy']:.6f} "
        f"score={final_metrics['score']:.6f}",
        flush=True,
    )
    return {
        "config": asdict(config),
        "metrics": final_metrics,
        "results": [asdict(r) for r in results],
    }


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="MLS-Bench synth-dnf task.")
    p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    p.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--label", type=str, default="eval")
    p.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--n-features", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--num-terms", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--term-width", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--monotone", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--sparse-subset", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--train-size", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--test-size", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--num-targets", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--num-trainsets", type=int, default=None)
    return p.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    config = maybe_apply_smoke_mode(DEFAULT_TASK, args.smoke)
    overrides: dict[str, object] = {}
    if args.n_features is not None:
        overrides["n_features"] = args.n_features
    if args.num_terms is not None:
        overrides["num_terms"] = args.num_terms
    if args.term_width is not None:
        overrides["term_width"] = args.term_width
    if args.monotone:
        overrides["monotone"] = True
    if args.sparse_subset is not None:
        overrides["sparse_subset"] = args.sparse_subset
    if args.train_size is not None:
        overrides["train_size"] = args.train_size
    if args.test_size is not None:
        overrides["test_size"] = args.test_size
    if args.num_targets is not None:
        overrides["num_targets"] = args.num_targets
    if args.num_trainsets is not None:
        overrides["num_trainsets"] = args.num_trainsets
    if overrides:
        config = replace(config, **overrides)
    summary = run_benchmark(config=config, seed=args.seed)
    if args.output_dir is not None:
        args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out = args.output_dir / f"{args.label}_seed{args.seed}.json"
        out.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))

def build_model(config: TaskConfig, seed: int):
    """2-hidden-layer MLP (256, 256) with ReLU."""

    from torch import nn

    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    hidden = 256
    model = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(config.n_features, hidden),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(hidden, hidden),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(hidden, 1),
    )
    return model, {"kind": "mlp", "hidden": hidden}


def make_dataset(
    dnf: tuple[tuple[tuple[int, int], ...], ...],
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,

    """Uniform Boolean training set."""
    x = make_uniform_examples(config, config.train_size, seed)
    y = evaluate_dnf(x, dnf)
    return x, y


def fit_and_predict(
    model,
    info: dict,
    train_x: np.ndarray,
    train_y: np.ndarray,
    test_x: np.ndarray,
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """AdamW + BCE training, 20 epochs."""
    import torch
    from torch import nn

    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    model = model.to(device)
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)
    criterion = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()

    train_x_t = torch.from_numpy(train_x).float().to(device)
    train_y_t = torch.from_numpy(train_y).float().to(device)
    test_x_t = torch.from_numpy(test_x).float().to(device)

    epochs = 20
    batch_size = 256
    n = train_x_t.shape[0]
    model.train()
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        perm = torch.randperm(n, device=device)
        for start in range(0, n, batch_size):
            idx = perm[start : start + batch_size]
            logits = model(train_x_t[idx]).view(-1)
            loss = criterion(logits, train_y_t[idx])
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
        if (epoch + 1) % 5 == 0 or epoch == 0:
            with torch.no_grad():
                tr_acc = (
                    ((torch.sigmoid(model(train_x_t)).view(-1) >= 0.5).long()
                     == train_y_t.long()).float().mean().item()
                )
            print(
                f"TRAIN_METRICS epoch={epoch + 1} loss={loss.item():.4f} train_acc={tr_acc:.4f}",
                flush=True,
            )
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        preds = (torch.sigmoid(model(test_x_t)).view(-1) >= 0.5).long().cpu().numpy()
    return preds

def build_model(config: TaskConfig, seed: int):
    """Neural Logic Network with soft literal selection and noisy-OR output."""
    import torch
    from torch import nn

    torch.manual_seed(seed)

    class NeuralDNF(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, n_features: int, n_terms: int):
            super().__init__()
            self.literal_logits = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(n_terms, n_features, 3))
            self.term_logits = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(n_terms))
            self.out_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1))
            self.n_features = n_features
            self.n_terms = n_terms
            self.reset_parameters()

        def reset_parameters(self) -> None:
            with torch.no_grad():
                self.literal_logits[..., 0].fill_(-4.0)  # positive literal
                self.literal_logits[..., 1].fill_(-4.0)  # negative literal
                self.literal_logits[..., 2].fill_(4.0)   # skip literal
                self.literal_logits.add_(0.03 * torch.randn_like(self.literal_logits))
                self.term_logits.fill_(-3.0)
                self.out_bias.zero_()

        def initialize_terms(self, terms: list[tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]) -> None:
            self.reset_parameters()
            with torch.no_grad():
                for term_index, (variables, polarities) in enumerate(terms[: self.n_terms]):
                    self.term_logits[term_index] = 2.5
                    for var, pol in zip(variables, polarities):
                        self.literal_logits[term_index, int(var), :].fill_(-5.0)
                        self.literal_logits[term_index, int(var), 2] = -5.0
                        self.literal_logits[term_index, int(var), 0 if int(pol) == 1 else 1] = 5.0

        def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            probs = torch.softmax(self.literal_logits, dim=-1)
            pos = probs[..., 0]
            neg = probs[..., 1]
            skip = probs[..., 2]
            literal = (
                pos.unsqueeze(0) * x.unsqueeze(1)
                + neg.unsqueeze(0) * (1.0 - x.unsqueeze(1))
                + skip.unsqueeze(0)
            ).clamp(min=1e-6, max=1.0)
            conj = torch.exp(torch.log(literal).sum(dim=-1)).clamp(max=1.0)
            term_prob = torch.sigmoid(self.term_logits).unsqueeze(0) * conj
            log_not = torch.log1p(-term_prob.clamp(max=1.0 - 1e-6)).sum(dim=-1)
            prob = (1.0 - torch.exp(log_not)).clamp(min=1e-6, max=1.0 - 1e-6)
            return torch.log(prob) - torch.log1p(-prob) + self.out_bias

        def literal_usage(self) -> torch.Tensor:
            probs = torch.softmax(self.literal_logits, dim=-1)
            return (probs[..., 0] + probs[..., 1]).sum(dim=-1)

    n_terms = max(4 * config.num_terms, 32)
    model = NeuralDNF(config.n_features, n_terms)
    return model, {"kind": "neural_dnf", "n_terms": n_terms}


def make_dataset(
    dnf: tuple[tuple[tuple[int, int], ...], ...],
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Uniform Boolean training set."""
    x = make_uniform_examples(config, config.train_size, seed)
    y = evaluate_dnf(x, dnf)
    return x, y


def _mine_candidate_terms(
    train_x: np.ndarray,
    train_y: np.ndarray,
    config: TaskConfig,
    max_terms: int,
    seed: int,
) -> list[tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]:
    """Data-driven initialization for a soft DNF layer."""
    from itertools import combinations, product

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    x = train_x.astype(np.int8, copy=False)
    y = train_y.astype(bool, copy=False)
    if y.sum() == 0 or (~y).sum() == 0:
        return []

    pos_mean = x[y].mean(axis=0)
    neg_mean = x[~y].mean(axis=0)
    variable_score = np.abs(pos_mean - neg_mean)
    if config.monotone:
        top_m = min(config.n_features, 30)
    elif config.sparse_subset > 0:
        top_m = min(config.n_features, max(config.sparse_subset + 4, 16))
    else:
        top_m = min(config.n_features, 18)
    top_vars = np.argsort(variable_score)[-top_m:]

    combos = np.array(list(combinations(top_vars.tolist(), config.term_width)), dtype=np.int64)
    if combos.size == 0:
        return []
    if config.monotone:
        patterns = np.ones((1, config.term_width), dtype=np.int8)
    else:
        patterns = np.array(list(product([0, 1], repeat=config.term_width)), dtype=np.int8)
    vars_arr = np.repeat(combos, len(patterns), axis=0)
    pols_arr = np.tile(patterns, (len(combos), 1))

    max_candidates = 36000
    if len(vars_arr) > max_candidates:
        keep = rng.choice(len(vars_arr), size=max_candidates, replace=False)
        vars_arr = vars_arr[keep]
        pols_arr = pols_arr[keep]

    scores = np.empty(len(vars_arr), dtype=np.float64)
    chunk = 512
    pos_count = max(int(y.sum()), 1)
    for start in range(0, len(vars_arr), chunk):
        end = min(start + chunk, len(vars_arr))
        v = vars_arr[start:end]
        p = pols_arr[start:end]
        match = np.ones((x.shape[0], end - start), dtype=bool)
        for j in range(config.term_width):
            match &= x[:, v[:, j]] == p[:, j]
        covered = match.sum(axis=0)
        pos_covered = match[y].sum(axis=0)
        precision = pos_covered / np.maximum(covered, 1)
        recall = pos_covered / pos_count
        chunk_scores = precision + 0.25 * recall
        chunk_scores[covered < 4] = -1.0
        scores[start:end] = chunk_scores

    order = np.argsort(scores)[::-1]
    selected: list[tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]] = []
    seen: set[tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]] = set()
    for idx in order:
        if scores[idx] <= 0:
            break
        term_key = tuple(sorted((int(v), int(p)) for v, p in zip(vars_arr[idx], pols_arr[idx])))
        if term_key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(term_key)
        selected.append((vars_arr[idx].copy(), pols_arr[idx].copy()))
        if len(selected) >= max_terms:
            break
    return selected


def fit_and_predict(
    model,
    info: dict,
    train_x: np.ndarray,
    train_y: np.ndarray,
    test_x: np.ndarray,
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    import torch
    from torch import nn

    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    terms = _mine_candidate_terms(train_x, train_y, config, info.get("n_terms", 32), seed)
    if hasattr(model, "initialize_terms"):
        model.initialize_terms(terms)

    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    model = model.to(device)
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=2e-3, weight_decay=1e-5)
    criterion = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()

    train_x_t = torch.from_numpy(train_x).float().to(device)
    train_y_t = torch.from_numpy(train_y).float().to(device)
    test_x_t = torch.from_numpy(test_x).float().to(device)

    epochs = 30
    batch_size = 512
    n = train_x_t.shape[0]
    target_width = float(config.term_width)
    model.train()
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        perm = torch.randperm(n, device=device)
        for start in range(0, n, batch_size):
            idx = perm[start : start + batch_size]
            logits = model(train_x_t[idx]).view(-1)
            loss = criterion(logits, train_y_t[idx])
            usage = model.literal_usage()
            width_penalty = ((usage - target_width).clamp(min=0.0) ** 2).mean()
            gate_penalty = torch.sigmoid(model.term_logits).mean()
            total = loss + 1e-4 * width_penalty + 1e-4 * gate_penalty
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            total.backward()
            optimizer.step()
        if (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0 or epoch == 0:
            with torch.no_grad():
                pred = (model(train_x_t).view(-1) >= 0.0).long()
                tr_acc = (pred == train_y_t.long()).float().mean().item()
            print(
                f"TRAIN_METRICS epoch={epoch + 1} loss={loss.item():.4f} "
                f"terms={len(terms)} train_acc={tr_acc:.4f}",
                flush=True,
            )
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        preds = (model(test_x_t).view(-1) >= 0.0).long().cpu().numpy()
    return preds

tasks.name: Length-Generalizing Dyck Stack Model
tasks.summary: Studies how sequence architectures implement stack-like memory for bounded Dyck languages and length-out-of-distribution generalization.
tasks.description_md:
# Synthetic: Dyck-(k,m) Language Modelling

## Research Question
Can you design a sequence-model architecture that learns the **bounded
hierarchical Dyck-(k,m) language** — well-nested strings over `k` bracket
types with maximum nesting depth `m` — and, crucially, that
**length-generalizes** to test strings strictly longer than anything seen
during training?

## Background
Dyck-(k,m) is the canonical formal language for studying whether neural
sequence models can implement an *explicit stack*.  At every position of a
Dyck string the next valid tokens are determined entirely by the stack of
currently-open brackets, so an exact recognizer needs only `O(m log k)`
bits of memory (Hewitt, Hahn, Ganguli, Liang, Manning, EMNLP 2020,
[arXiv:2010.07515](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07515)).  Yet vanilla LSTMs
and Transformers regularly fail to length-generalize on Dyck-(k,m): they
collapse from near-100% accuracy on in-distribution lengths down to
chance on longer test strings.  Adding an explicit differentiable stack
(Joulin & Mikolov, NeurIPS 2015, [arXiv:1503.01007](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.01007);
Suzgun et al. 2019, [arXiv:1911.03329](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.03329))
or a carefully designed positional encoding (Yao, Peng, Papadimitriou,
Narasimhan, ACL 2021, [arXiv:2105.11115](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.11115))
restores generalization.  This task asks the agent to invent the
architectural fix.

## What You Can Modify
Edit only the `build_model(...)` function inside the editable block of
`pytorch-examples/synth_dyck/custom_strategy.py`.  Everything else —
the Dyck-(k,m) sampler, the vocabulary, the language-model training
loop (AdamW, cross-entropy on every position, gradient clipping), the
evaluation (next-valid-set token accuracy + per-string accuracy), and
the per-environment overrides — is fixed.

## Fixed Setup
- **Vocabulary** (size `2k + 2`): BOS, EOS/PAD, `k` open brackets, `k`
  matching close brackets.
- **Training corpus**: 8 000 strings sampled uniformly over even lengths
  in the per-environment training range, kept in memory.
- **Evaluation corpora**: 1 000 in-distribution strings (same length
  range as training) and 1 000 length-OOD strings (lengths strictly
  longer than the training maximum).
- **Loss**: token-level softmax cross-entropy over non-PAD positions.
- **Optimizer**: AdamW, `lr = 3e-3`, `weight_decay = 0`, gradient norm
  clipped to `1.0`.
- **Batch size**: 64.
- **Training budget**: 100 gradient steps per env.
- **Parameter budget**: `≤ 500 000` trainable parameters
  (`config.max_params`).  The harness raises an error if `build_model`
  exceeds this.
- **Runs per env**: 1 internal run per outer seed.

## Interface
`build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> DyckModel` must return a
`torch.nn.Module` subclass of `DyckModel` that exposes
`forward(input_ids: LongTensor[B, T]) -> logits: FloatTensor[B, T, vocab]`.
The model receives sequences of the form `[BOS, x1, …, xn, EOS, PAD, …]`
and is scored on its predictions at every non-PAD position.

## Fixed Setup
| label              | `k` | `m` | train length | OOD eval length |
|--------------------|-----|-----|--------------|-----------------|
| `dyck-k2-m3`       | 2   | 3   | [8, 64]      | [65, 96]        |
| `dyck-k8-m5`       | 8   | 5   | [16, 96]     | [97, 128]       |
| `dyck-length-ood`  | 4   | 4   | [8, 64]      | [128, 256]      |

The third environment is the hard length-OOD probe: training tops out
at length 64 and the model is tested on strings of length 128–256.

## Metrics
For each environment the parser writes the following columns to the
leaderboard:
- `id_token_acc_<env>` — token-level next-valid-set accuracy on the
  in-distribution split (higher is better, bounded in `[0, 1]`).
- `ood_token_acc_<env>` — same metric on the length-OOD split (this is
  the **headline** generalization score and the primary score column).
- `id_string_acc_<env>`, `ood_string_acc_<env>` — strict per-string
  accuracy (every position correct).
- `params_<env>` — number of trainable parameters reported by
  `MODEL_INFO`.

Per-env scores use `ood_token_acc`; the task score is the geometric mean
across the three environments.

## Baselines
1. **`lstm`** — 2-layer LSTM language model (Hewitt et al. EMNLP 2020,
   [arXiv:2010.07515](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.07515)).
2. **`transformer`** — 4-layer causal Transformer with learned absolute
   positional embeddings (Yao et al. ACL 2021,
   [arXiv:2105.11115](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.11115)).
3. **`stack_rnn`** — Stack-augmented RNN with softmax PUSH/POP/NO-OP
   actions, following Joulin & Mikolov, NeurIPS 2015
   ([arXiv:1503.01007](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.01007)) and the
   `Stack-RNN+Softmax` variant of Suzgun et al. 2019
   ([arXiv:1911.03329](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.03329)).

Background

Dyck-(k,m) is the canonical formal language for studying whether neural sequence models can implement an explicit stack. At every position of a Dyck string the next valid tokens are determined entirely by the stack of currently-open brackets, so an exact recognizer needs only O(m log k) bits of memory (Hewitt, Hahn, Ganguli, Liang, Manning, EMNLP 2020, arXiv:2010.07515). Yet vanilla LSTMs and Transformers regularly fail to length-generalize on Dyck-(k,m): they collapse from near-100% accuracy on in-distribution lengths down to chance on longer test strings. Adding an explicit differentiable stack (Joulin & Mikolov, NeurIPS 2015, arXiv:1503.01007; Suzgun et al. 2019, arXiv:1911.03329) or a carefully designed positional encoding (Yao, Peng, Papadimitriou, Narasimhan, ACL 2021, arXiv:2105.11115) restores generalization. This task asks the agent to invent the architectural fix.

What You Can Modify

Edit only the build_model(...) function inside the editable block of pytorch-examples/synth_dyck/custom_strategy.py. Everything else — the Dyck-(k,m) sampler, the vocabulary, the language-model training loop (AdamW, cross-entropy on every position, gradient clipping), the evaluation (next-valid-set token accuracy + per-string accuracy), and the per-environment overrides — is fixed.

Fixed Setup

  • Vocabulary (size 2k + 2): BOS, EOS/PAD, k open brackets, k matching close brackets.
  • Training corpus: 8 000 strings sampled uniformly over even lengths in the per-environment training range, kept in memory.
  • Evaluation corpora: 1 000 in-distribution strings (same length range as training) and 1 000 length-OOD strings (lengths strictly longer than the training maximum).
  • Loss: token-level softmax cross-entropy over non-PAD positions.
  • Optimizer: AdamW, lr = 3e-3, weight_decay = 0, gradient norm clipped to 1.0.
  • Batch size: 64.
  • Training budget: 100 gradient steps per env.
  • Parameter budget: ≤ 500 000 trainable parameters (config.max_params). The harness raises an error if build_model exceeds this.
  • Runs per env: 1 internal run per outer seed.

Interface

build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> DyckModel must return a torch.nn.Module subclass of DyckModel that exposes forward(input_ids: LongTensor[B, T]) -> logits: FloatTensor[B, T, vocab]. The model receives sequences of the form [BOS, x1, …, xn, EOS, PAD, …] and is scored on its predictions at every non-PAD position.

Fixed Setup

label k m train length OOD eval length
dyck-k2-m3 2 3 [8, 64] [65, 96]
dyck-k8-m5 8 5 [16, 96] [97, 128]
dyck-length-ood 4 4 [8, 64] [128, 256]

The third environment is the hard length-OOD probe: training tops out at length 64 and the model is tested on strings of length 128–256.

Metrics

For each environment the parser writes the following columns to the leaderboard: - id_token_acc_<env> — token-level next-valid-set accuracy on the in-distribution split (higher is better, bounded in [0, 1]). - ood_token_acc_<env> — same metric on the length-OOD split (this is the headline generalization score and the primary score column). - id_string_acc_<env>, ood_string_acc_<env> — strict per-string accuracy (every position correct). - params_<env> — number of trainable parameters reported by MODEL_INFO.

Per-env scores use ood_token_acc; the task score is the geometric mean across the three environments.

Baselines

  1. lstm — 2-layer LSTM language model (Hewitt et al. EMNLP 2020, arXiv:2010.07515).
  2. transformer — 4-layer causal Transformer with learned absolute positional embeddings (Yao et al. ACL 2021, arXiv:2105.11115).
  3. stack_rnn — Stack-augmented RNN with softmax PUSH/POP/NO-OP actions, following Joulin & Mikolov, NeurIPS 2015 (arXiv:1503.01007) and the Stack-RNN+Softmax variant of Suzgun et al. 2019 (arXiv:1911.03329).
