"""Dyck-(k,m) language-modelling scaffold for MLS-Bench.

The agent's job is to design a sequence model that learns the bounded
hierarchical Dyck-(k,m) language: well-nested strings over k bracket types
with maximum nesting depth m.  The data generator, training loop, optimizer
choice, and evaluation protocol are FIXED.  The agent only controls

    * `build_model(...)` — the sequence model constructor.

The model is trained as a left-to-right language model: at every position the
model must place all of its probability mass on the set of *valid* next
tokens (the union of open brackets at non-max depth and the closing bracket
that matches the current top of the stack).  We report the standard
"constraint-satisfaction" / "next-valid-set" accuracy from Hewitt et al.
(EMNLP 2020) — at each timestep the prediction is correct iff the top-1
token is in the valid set.  In-distribution accuracy uses test lengths
drawn from the same distribution as training; length-OOD accuracy uses
test lengths strictly longer than the training maximum.

References:
  Hewitt, Hahn, Ganguli, Liang, Manning, "RNNs can generate bounded
    hierarchical languages with optimal memory", EMNLP 2020
    (arXiv:2010.07515).
  Suzgun et al. 2019, "Memory-Augmented Recurrent Neural Networks Can Learn
    Generalized Dyck Languages" (arXiv:1911.03329).
  Yao, Peng, Papadimitriou, Narasimhan, "Self-Attention Networks Can Process
    Bounded Hierarchical Languages", ACL 2021 (arXiv:2105.11115).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import random
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable

import torch
from torch import nn


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Benchmark configuration
# =====================================================================
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskConfig:
    # Language parameters
    k: int = 2                       # number of bracket types
    m: int = 3                       # maximum nesting depth
    train_min_len: int = 8           # minimum training-string length (tokens)
    train_max_len: int = 64          # maximum training-string length (tokens)
    test_max_len: int = 64           # maximum in-distribution test length
    ood_max_len: int = 64            # maximum length-OOD test length (set per env)
    ood_min_len: int = 65            # minimum length-OOD test length (set per env)

    # Dataset / training parameters
    train_size: int = 8_000          # number of training strings
    eval_size: int = 1_000           # number of in-distribution eval strings
    ood_size: int = 1_000            # number of length-OOD eval strings
    batch_size: int = 64
    max_steps: int = 4_000           # gradient steps (epochs cycle the train set)
    lr: float = 3e-3
    weight_decay: float = 0.0
    grad_clip: float = 1.0
    log_interval: int = 1000

    # Model budget (advisory)
    hidden_dim: int = 64
    max_params: int = 500_000        # rejected if build_model exceeds this


DEFAULT_TASK = TaskConfig()

# Vocabulary layout (size = 2k + 2):
#   0          : BOS / start-of-sequence
#   1          : EOS  (also used as PAD; loss masks PAD positions)
#   2 .. k+1   : open brackets  '(', '[', '{', ...   (one per bracket type)
#   k+2 .. 2k+1: close brackets ')', ']', '}', ...   (matches by index)
def vocab_size(k: int) -> int:
    return 2 * k + 2


def open_id(k: int, t: int) -> int:
    """Token id of the t-th open bracket (0 <= t < k)."""
    return 2 + t


def close_id(k: int, t: int) -> int:
    """Token id of the t-th closing bracket (0 <= t < k)."""
    return 2 + k + t


def is_open(token: int, k: int) -> bool:
    return 2 <= token < 2 + k


def is_close(token: int, k: int) -> bool:
    return 2 + k <= token < 2 + 2 * k


BOS_ID = 0
EOS_ID = 1
PAD_ID = 1  # We reuse EOS as the padding token; loss masks PAD positions.


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Dyck-(k,m) string sampling and validity oracle
# =====================================================================
def sample_dyck_string(
    k: int,
    m: int,
    min_len: int,
    max_len: int,
    rng: random.Random,
) -> list[int]:
    """Sample a single Dyck-(k,m) string of even length in [min_len, max_len].

    Uses a depth-bounded random walk: at each position pick either an open
    bracket (allowed when depth < m and at least 2 tokens remain to close)
    or a closing bracket (allowed when depth > 0).  Length is fixed up
    front by sampling an even value in the allowed range.
    """
    if min_len % 2:
        min_len += 1
    if max_len % 2:
        max_len -= 1
    if max_len < min_len:
        raise ValueError("Empty length range for Dyck sampler.")
    # Length is sampled uniformly over the allowed even values.
    half = rng.randrange(min_len // 2, max_len // 2 + 1)
    length = 2 * half

    tokens: list[int] = []
    stack: list[int] = []  # holds bracket type ids that need closing
    remaining = length
    for _ in range(length):
        depth = len(stack)
        # Number of tokens left to emit after this one.
        rest = remaining - 1
        # Must close enough to drain the stack; cannot open without leaving
        # room for the matching close.
        can_open = depth < m and rest >= depth + 1
        can_close = depth > 0
        if can_open and can_close:
            # Bias slightly toward opening so we explore deeper nesting.
            open_prob = 0.55 if depth < m - 1 else 0.45
            do_open = rng.random() < open_prob
        elif can_open:
            do_open = True
        elif can_close:
            do_open = False
        else:
            raise RuntimeError("Dyck sampler stuck — invariants violated.")
        if do_open:
            t = rng.randrange(k)
            tokens.append(open_id(k, t))
            stack.append(t)
        else:
            t = stack.pop()
            tokens.append(close_id(k, t))
        remaining -= 1
    if stack:
        raise RuntimeError("Dyck sampler ended with non-empty stack.")
    return tokens


def valid_next_set(prefix: list[int], k: int, m: int) -> set[int]:
    """Return the set of valid next-token ids given the prefix of a Dyck-(k,m)
    string (prefix may include BOS).  EOS is valid iff the stack is empty.
    """
    stack: list[int] = []
    for tok in prefix:
        if tok == BOS_ID:
            continue
        if tok == EOS_ID:
            return set()
        if is_open(tok, k):
            stack.append(tok - 2)
        elif is_close(tok, k):
            close_type = tok - (2 + k)
            if not stack or stack[-1] != close_type:
                return set()
            stack.pop()
        else:
            return set()
    depth = len(stack)
    allowed: set[int] = set()
    if depth < m:
        for t in range(k):
            allowed.add(open_id(k, t))
    if depth > 0:
        allowed.add(close_id(k, stack[-1]))
    else:
        allowed.add(EOS_ID)
    return allowed


def encode_batch(
    strings: list[list[int]],
    pad_to: int,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Pack a batch of token lists into (input_ids, target_ids, mask).

    Each example is BOS x1 x2 ... xn EOS, padded to `pad_to + 2`.  The model
    sees positions [BOS, x1, ..., xn] and predicts [x1, ..., xn, EOS].
    `mask` is 1 on positions that contribute to the loss.
    """
    full_len = pad_to + 2
    inp = torch.full((len(strings), full_len), PAD_ID, dtype=torch.long)
    tgt = torch.full((len(strings), full_len), PAD_ID, dtype=torch.long)
    mask = torch.zeros((len(strings), full_len), dtype=torch.bool)
    for row, s in enumerate(strings):
        seq = [BOS_ID] + list(s) + [EOS_ID]
        # input: positions 0 .. len(seq)-2; target: positions 1 .. len(seq)-1
        n_pred = len(seq) - 1
        inp[row, :n_pred] = torch.tensor(seq[:-1], dtype=torch.long)
        tgt[row, :n_pred] = torch.tensor(seq[1:], dtype=torch.long)
        mask[row, :n_pred] = True
    return inp, tgt, mask


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: pre-sampled dataset wrappers
# =====================================================================
@dataclass
class DyckSplit:
    strings: list[list[int]]
    pad_to: int

    def loader(self, batch_size: int, shuffle: bool, rng: random.Random) -> Iterable:
        indices = list(range(len(self.strings)))
        if shuffle:
            rng.shuffle(indices)
        for start in range(0, len(indices), batch_size):
            chunk = indices[start : start + batch_size]
            batch = [self.strings[i] for i in chunk]
            yield encode_batch(batch, pad_to=self.pad_to)


def build_dataset(config: TaskConfig, seed: int) -> tuple[DyckSplit, DyckSplit, DyckSplit]:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    train = [
        sample_dyck_string(config.k, config.m, config.train_min_len, config.train_max_len, rng)
        for _ in range(config.train_size)
    ]
    eval_rng = random.Random(seed + 1)
    eval_id = [
        sample_dyck_string(config.k, config.m, config.train_min_len, config.test_max_len, eval_rng)
        for _ in range(config.eval_size)
    ]
    ood_rng = random.Random(seed + 2)
    ood = [
        sample_dyck_string(config.k, config.m, config.ood_min_len, config.ood_max_len, ood_rng)
        for _ in range(config.ood_size)
    ]
    return (
        DyckSplit(strings=train, pad_to=config.train_max_len),
        DyckSplit(strings=eval_id, pad_to=config.test_max_len),
        DyckSplit(strings=ood, pad_to=config.ood_max_len),
    )


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: model API contract
# =====================================================================
class DyckModel(nn.Module):
    """Interface that `build_model` must return.

    The model is a left-to-right language model over the Dyck vocabulary.
    It must implement `forward(input_ids) -> logits` where `input_ids` has
    shape `[batch, seq_len]` and `logits` has shape `[batch, seq_len, vocab]`.
    The training loop applies softmax cross-entropy at every non-PAD
    position; the evaluator computes next-valid-set accuracy from the
    argmax of `logits`.
    """

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:  # pragma: no cover
        raise NotImplementedError


# =====================================================================
# EDITABLE: build_model — the agent's full design space.
# Lines below this banner (until the matching FIXED banner) may be edited.
# =====================================================================
def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> DyckModel:
    """Construct the sequence model.

    Default baseline: a 2-layer LSTM language model with `config.hidden_dim`
    hidden units.  The agent is free to replace this entirely (e.g. with a
    Transformer, a stack-augmented RNN, or a memory network) as long as the
    returned module implements `DyckModel.forward(input_ids) -> logits`.
    """

    class LSTMModel(DyckModel):
        def __init__(self, vocab: int, hidden: int, num_layers: int):
            super().__init__()
            self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab, hidden)
            self.rnn = nn.LSTM(hidden, hidden, num_layers=num_layers, batch_first=True)
            self.head = nn.Linear(hidden, vocab)

        def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            h = self.embed(input_ids)
            h, _ = self.rnn(h)
            return self.head(h)

    return LSTMModel(vocab=vocab_size(config.k), hidden=config.hidden_dim, num_layers=2)


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: training and evaluation driver
# =====================================================================
def count_parameters(model: nn.Module) -> int:
    return sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)


def set_global_seed(seed: int) -> None:
    random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


def evaluate_next_valid(
    model: DyckModel,
    split: DyckSplit,
    config: TaskConfig,
    device: torch.device,
    batch_size: int,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Compute next-valid-set accuracy and per-string accuracy.

    A position is *correct* iff argmax(logits) at that position is contained
    in the valid next-token set computed from the gold prefix.  We report
    token-level accuracy (over non-PAD positions) and string-level accuracy
    (a string is correct iff every position is correct).
    """
    model.eval()
    rng = random.Random(0)  # deterministic order
    token_correct = 0
    token_total = 0
    string_correct = 0
    string_total = 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for input_ids, _target_ids, mask in split.loader(batch_size, shuffle=False, rng=rng):
            input_ids = input_ids.to(device)
            mask = mask.to(device)
            logits = model(input_ids)
            preds = logits.argmax(dim=-1)  # [B, T]
            # Build per-batch valid-next masks from the gold prefixes
            B, T = input_ids.shape
            for b in range(B):
                prefix: list[int] = []
                all_ok = True
                # input_ids[b] is [BOS, x1, ..., xn, PAD...]; we score positions
                # where mask[b, t] is True.
                for t in range(T):
                    if not bool(mask[b, t].item()):
                        break
                    prefix.append(int(input_ids[b, t].item()))
                    allowed = valid_next_set(prefix, config.k, config.m)
                    pred = int(preds[b, t].item())
                    if pred in allowed:
                        token_correct += 1
                    else:
                        all_ok = False
                    token_total += 1
                string_total += 1
                if all_ok:
                    string_correct += 1
    return {
        "token_accuracy": token_correct / max(token_total, 1),
        "string_accuracy": string_correct / max(string_total, 1),
        "token_total": float(token_total),
        "string_total": float(string_total),
    }


def train_one_run(
    config: TaskConfig,
    device: torch.device,
    seed: int,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    set_global_seed(seed)
    t0 = time.time()
    train_split, id_split, ood_split = build_dataset(config, seed=seed)

    model = build_model(config).to(device)
    if not isinstance(model, nn.Module):
        raise TypeError("build_model must return an nn.Module subclass of DyckModel.")
    n_params = count_parameters(model)
    if n_params > config.max_params:
        raise ValueError(
            f"build_model returned {n_params} parameters; budget is {config.max_params}."
        )
    print(
        f"MODEL_INFO params={n_params} vocab={vocab_size(config.k)} "
        f"k={config.k} m={config.m}",
        flush=True,
    )

    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        model.parameters(), lr=config.lr, weight_decay=config.weight_decay
    )
    loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction="none")

    rng = random.Random(seed + 99)
    steps = 0
    window_loss = 0.0
    window_count = 0
    while steps < config.max_steps:
        for input_ids, target_ids, mask in train_split.loader(
            config.batch_size, shuffle=True, rng=rng
        ):
            if steps >= config.max_steps:
                break
            model.train()
            input_ids = input_ids.to(device)
            target_ids = target_ids.to(device)
            mask = mask.to(device)
            logits = model(input_ids)
            B, T, V = logits.shape
            losses = loss_fn(logits.reshape(B * T, V), target_ids.reshape(B * T))
            losses = losses.reshape(B, T) * mask.float()
            denom = mask.float().sum().clamp_min(1.0)
            loss = losses.sum() / denom
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss.backward()
            if config.grad_clip > 0:
                nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), config.grad_clip)
            optimizer.step()
            window_loss += float(loss.item())
            window_count += 1
            steps += 1
            if steps == 1 or steps % config.log_interval == 0 or steps == config.max_steps:
                avg = window_loss / max(window_count, 1)
                print(
                    f"TRAIN_METRICS step={steps} loss={avg:.6f}",
                    flush=True,
                )
                window_loss = 0.0
                window_count = 0
    train_elapsed = time.time() - t0

    id_metrics = evaluate_next_valid(
        model, id_split, config, device, batch_size=config.batch_size
    )
    ood_metrics = evaluate_next_valid(
        model, ood_split, config, device, batch_size=config.batch_size
    )
    print(
        "EVAL_METRICS "
        f"id_token_acc={id_metrics['token_accuracy']:.6f} "
        f"id_string_acc={id_metrics['string_accuracy']:.6f} "
        f"ood_token_acc={ood_metrics['token_accuracy']:.6f} "
        f"ood_string_acc={ood_metrics['string_accuracy']:.6f} "
        f"params={n_params} train_seconds={train_elapsed:.1f}",
        flush=True,
    )

    return {
        "id_token_acc": id_metrics["token_accuracy"],
        "id_string_acc": id_metrics["string_accuracy"],
        "ood_token_acc": ood_metrics["token_accuracy"],
        "ood_string_acc": ood_metrics["string_accuracy"],
        "params": float(n_params),
        "train_seconds": float(train_elapsed),
    }


def resolve_device(device_arg: str) -> torch.device:
    if device_arg == "cpu":
        return torch.device("cpu")
    if device_arg == "cuda":
        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
            raise RuntimeError("CUDA requested but no GPU is available.")
        return torch.device("cuda")
    return torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")


def run_benchmark(config: TaskConfig, seed: int, device: torch.device) -> dict[str, object]:
    print(
        "TASK_CONFIG "
        + " ".join(
            [
                f"k={config.k}",
                f"m={config.m}",
                f"train_max_len={config.train_max_len}",
                f"test_max_len={config.test_max_len}",
                f"ood_min_len={config.ood_min_len}",
                f"ood_max_len={config.ood_max_len}",
                f"train_size={config.train_size}",
                f"max_steps={config.max_steps}",
                f"batch_size={config.batch_size}",
                f"lr={config.lr}",
                f"hidden_dim={config.hidden_dim}",
                f"max_params={config.max_params}",
            ]
        ),
        flush=True,
    )
    # One top-level runner seed maps to one dataset draw, init, and training run.
    num_runs = 1
    all_metrics: list[dict[str, float]] = []
    for r in range(num_runs):
        sub_seed = seed * 1_000 + r
        print(f"RUN_BEGIN run={r} sub_seed={sub_seed}", flush=True)
        result = train_one_run(config=config, device=device, seed=sub_seed)
        print(
            "RUN_METRICS "
            + " ".join(f"{k}={v:.6f}" for k, v in result.items()),
            flush=True,
        )
        all_metrics.append(result)

    def mean(name: str) -> float:
        return float(sum(d[name] for d in all_metrics) / len(all_metrics))

    def std(name: str) -> float:
        vals = [d[name] for d in all_metrics]
        mu = sum(vals) / len(vals)
        return float((sum((v - mu) ** 2 for v in vals) / len(vals)) ** 0.5)

    final = {
        "id_token_acc": mean("id_token_acc"),
        "id_string_acc": mean("id_string_acc"),
        "ood_token_acc": mean("ood_token_acc"),
        "ood_string_acc": mean("ood_string_acc"),
        "id_token_acc_std": std("id_token_acc"),
        "ood_token_acc_std": std("ood_token_acc"),
        "params": mean("params"),
        "num_runs": float(len(all_metrics)),
    }
    print(
        "FINAL_METRICS "
        + " ".join(
            f"{k}={v:.6f}" if isinstance(v, float) else f"{k}={v}"
            for k, v in final.items()
        ),
        flush=True,
    )
    print(
        "TEST_METRICS "
        f"id_token_acc={final['id_token_acc']:.6f} "
        f"id_string_acc={final['id_string_acc']:.6f} "
        f"ood_token_acc={final['ood_token_acc']:.6f} "
        f"ood_string_acc={final['ood_string_acc']:.6f}",
        flush=True,
    )
    return {"config": asdict(config), "metrics": final, "runs": all_metrics}


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="MLS-Bench synth-dyck task.")
    p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    p.add_argument("--label", type=str, default="eval")
    p.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--device", choices=("auto", "cpu", "cuda"), default="auto")
    # Per-environment overrides — these are the ONLY benchmark axes the
    # external script may change.  Internal training hyperparameters above
    # are fixed across environments.
    p.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--m", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--train-min-len", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--train-max-len", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--test-max-len", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--ood-min-len", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--ood-max-len", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=None)
    return p.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    cfg = DEFAULT_TASK

    if args.k is not None:

    if args.m is not None:
        overrides["m"] = args.m
    if args.train_min_len is not None:
        overrides["train_min_len"] = args.train_min_len
    if args.train_max_len is not None:
        overrides["train_max_len"] = args.train_max_len
        # Default OOD splits track the training maximum.
        if args.test_max_len is None:
            overrides["test_max_len"] = args.train_max_len
    if args.test_max_len is not None:
        overrides["test_max_len"] = args.test_max_len
    if args.ood_min_len is not None:
        overrides["ood_min_len"] = args.ood_min_len
    if args.ood_max_len is not None:

    if overrides:

def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> DyckModel:
    """4-layer causal Transformer with learned absolute positional embeddings."""

    class CausalTransformer(DyckModel):
        def __init__(self, vocab: int, hidden: int, num_layers: int, num_heads: int, max_len: int):
            super().__init__()
            self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab, hidden)
            self.pos = nn.Embedding(max_len, hidden)
            layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
                d_model=hidden,
                nhead=num_heads,
                dim_feedforward=4 * hidden,
                dropout=0.0,
                activation="gelu",
                batch_first=True,
                norm_first=True,
            )
            self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(layer, num_layers=num_layers)
            self.head = nn.Linear(hidden, vocab)
            self.register_buffer(
                "positions",
                torch.arange(max_len, dtype=torch.long).unsqueeze(0),
                persistent=False,
            )

        def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            B, T = input_ids.shape
            pos = self.positions[:, :T].expand(B, T)
            h = self.embed(input_ids) + self.pos(pos)
            causal = torch.triu(
                torch.full((T, T), float("-inf"), device=input_ids.device), diagonal=1,
            )
            h = self.encoder(h, mask=causal, is_causal=True)
            return self.head(h)

    # Cap max_len generously above any single-env requirement.
    return CausalTransformer(
        vocab=vocab_size(config.k),
        hidden=config.hidden_dim,
        num_layers=4,
        num_heads=4,
        max_len=1024,
    )

def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> DyckModel:
    """Stack-augmented RNN (Joulin & Mikolov 2015 + Softmax variant)."""

    class StackRNN(DyckModel):
        def __init__(self, vocab: int, hidden: int, stack_dim: int, stack_depth: int):
            super().__init__()
            self.hidden = hidden
            self.stack_dim = stack_dim
            self.stack_depth = stack_depth
            self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab, hidden)
            # Equivalent to an RNNCell over [embed, top_of_stack], but one
            # fused projection avoids two tiny matmuls per token.
            self.cell = nn.Linear(hidden + stack_dim + hidden, hidden)
            # 3-way action (PUSH / POP / NO-OP) plus new top candidate.
            self.stack_update = nn.Linear(hidden, 3 + stack_dim)
            self.head = nn.Linear(hidden + stack_dim, vocab)
            push_shift = torch.zeros(stack_depth, stack_depth)
            pop_shift = torch.zeros(stack_depth, stack_depth)
            if stack_depth > 1:
                eye = torch.eye(stack_depth - 1)
                push_shift[1:, :-1] = eye
                pop_shift[:-1, 1:] = eye
            top_slot = torch.zeros(1, stack_depth, 1)
            top_slot[:, 0, :] = 1.0
            self.register_buffer("push_shift", push_shift, persistent=False)
            self.register_buffer("pop_shift", pop_shift, persistent=False)
            self.register_buffer("top_slot", top_slot, persistent=False)

        def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            B, T = input_ids.shape
            device = input_ids.device
            h = torch.zeros(B, self.hidden, device=device)
            stack = torch.zeros(B, self.stack_depth, self.stack_dim, device=device)
            embeddings = self.embed(input_ids)
            states = []
            for t in range(T):
                emb = embeddings[:, t]
                top = stack[:, 0]
                h = torch.tanh(self.cell(torch.cat([emb, top, h], dim=-1)))
                update = self.stack_update(h)
                action_logits, push_raw = update[:, :3], update[:, 3:]
                a = torch.softmax(action_logits, dim=-1).view(B, 3, 1, 1)
                push_p, pop_p, noop_p = a[:, 0], a[:, 1], a[:, 2]
                new_top = torch.tanh(push_raw)

                pushed = torch.matmul(self.push_shift, stack) + self.top_slot * new_top.unsqueeze(1)
                popped = torch.matmul(self.pop_shift, stack)
                stack = push_p * pushed + pop_p * popped + noop_p * stack
                states.append(torch.cat([h, stack[:, 0]], dim=-1))
            return self.head(torch.stack(states, dim=1))

    return StackRNN(
        vocab=vocab_size(config.k),
        hidden=config.hidden_dim,
        stack_dim=config.hidden_dim,
        stack_depth=config.m + 2,
    )

tasks.summary: Studies how sequence architectures avoid rare read errors in flip-flop language modeling, especially on long sparse tails.
tasks.description_md:
# Synth Flip-Flop Language Modeling

## Research Question
Design a causal sequence-model architecture (or attention modification) that, with all training data, optimizer, and evaluation pipeline held fixed, **eliminates the rare-but-persistent read errors** that vanilla Transformers exhibit when modelling the flip-flop language of Liu et al. 2023 — especially on the **long sparse tail** of the input distribution.

## Background
The flip-flop language `FFL(T, p)` of Liu, Ash, Goel, Krishnamurthy, Zhang ("Exposing Attention Glitches with Flip-Flop Language Modeling", NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2306.00946) is the simplest non-trivial state-tracking language. Each token is a (instruction, bit) pair from
```
Sigma = { w0, w1, i0, i1, r0, r1 }
```
where
- `w b` writes bit `b` to a 1-bit memory;
- `i b` is an *ignore* with a random visible bit; the memory does not change;
- `r b` is a *read*: the second symbol `b` is constrained to be the current memory state, and the model is graded on whether it predicts the read bit correctly.

The triple `(p_w, p_r, p_i)` controls the distribution. The paper's canonical training distribution is `FFL(T=512, p_i=0.8)` (so `p_w = p_r = 0.1`). Out-of-distribution evaluation amplifies the rare tail behaviours:
- `FFL(p_i=0.98)` — sparse: long stretches of ignore, the read sees a write at a distance often > 100 tokens (the failure mode for vanilla Transformers).
- `FFL(p_i=0.5)` — dense: writes are common; the most-recent write is usually within a few tokens.
- A long-context variant (T = 1024) at the training distribution.

Liu et al. report that vanilla Transformers exhibit *attention glitches*: rare but persistent read errors whose probability does not vanish with scaling or with training data, while a 1-layer LSTM achieves **exactly 0 OOD error on 100/100 replicates** (Section B.2, result R2). Mamba-style state-space models inherit the same recurrent inductive bias (Gu & Dao 2023, arXiv:2312.00752) and trivially solve FFLM-class state-tracking; see also Mamba-3 (arXiv:2603.15569, Section on Parity).

## Task
Edit `pytorch-examples/synth_flip_flop/custom_strategy.py` **only inside the editable block** (the `class FlipFlopModel(nn.Module)` plus the `build_model(config)` factory, lines 191-241 of the scaffold). Everything else — data generation, training loop, optimizer, evaluation — is FIXED and must not be modified.

The fixed training loop runs for 3000 steps on freshly sampled `FFL(p_i=0.8, T=512)` batches with AdamW (lr=3e-4, wd=0.1, batch_size=16), then evaluates on three OOD splits.

## Interface
- Implement a `torch.nn.Module` whose `forward(tokens)` accepts a `LongTensor` of shape `[batch, seq_len]` (token ids in 0..5) and returns a `FloatTensor` of shape `[batch, seq_len, 6]` of next-token logits.
- The model **must be causal**: position `t` depends only on positions `<= t`.
- The model must handle sequence lengths up to 1024 (used for the long-context eval).
- Total trainable parameters should stay below 50M.
- Provide a `build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module` factory that the fixed driver calls.
- The model is graded on **read positions only**: a prediction is wrong iff `argmax(logits[t])` does not equal the read-bit target `tokens[t+1]` when `tokens[t+1] in {r0=4, r1=5}`. The headline metric is `seq_error_rate` = fraction of evaluation sequences with at least one read error; the `score` reported per environment is `1 - seq_error_rate`.

## Fixed Setup
- Vocab: `{w0=0, w1=1, i0=2, i1=3, r0=4, r1=5}` (6 tokens total).
- Training distribution: `FFL(T=512, p_i=0.8)`, online sampling.
- Optimizer: AdamW with `lr=3e-4, betas=(0.9, 0.999), wd=0.1, warmup=50, linear decay`.
- Batch size: 16, max steps: 3000, gradient clipping at 1.0.
- Loss: cross-entropy over the full next-token distribution at every position.
- Three OOD eval splits, each scored independently:
  - `dense` (`FFL(p_i=0.5, T=512)`, 2000 sequences)
  - `sparse` (`FFL(p_i=0.98, T=512)`, 2000 sequences) — the headline tail
  - `long_ctx` (`FFL(p_i=0.8, T=1024)`, 500 sequences)

## Metric
Per environment:
- `score = 1 - seq_error_rate` (higher is better, bounded in [0, 1])
- `read_error_rate` = errors / total reads (lower is better)
- `seq_error_rate` = sequences with >= 1 read error / total sequences (lower is better)

The overall task score is the geometric mean of the per-environment scores. The most interesting split is `sparse`, where Liu et al. (2023) document the vanilla-Transformer failure mode.

## Baselines (literature references)
- **transformer** — 4-layer, 8-head, d_model=256 vanilla causal Transformer. Mirrors the "canonical baseline" of Liu et al. (NeurIPS 2023, Section 4).
- **lstm** — 1-layer LSTM, hidden=128 (Liu et al. NeurIPS 2023, Section B.2 (R2)).
- **attn_sharp** — 4-layer Transformer with attention-sharpening (low-temperature softmax), cf. Liu et al. Section 4.2 / Figure 3 ("ent. attn sharp", "L attn sharp", "L2 attn sharp").
- **ssm** — Pure-PyTorch Mamba-style selective diagonal SSM (Gu & Dao 2023, arXiv:2312.00752).

"""Synth Flip-Flop Language Modeling scaffold for MLS-Bench.

Setup follows Liu, Ash, Goel, Krishnamurthy, Zhang, "Exposing Attention
Glitches with Flip-Flop Language Modeling" (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2306.00946).

The FFL(T, p) distribution emits length-T strings over the vocabulary
    Sigma = { w0, w1, r, i, 0, 1 }
where each step is a (instruction, value) pair:
  - "w 0" / "w 1": write the bit to a 1-bit memory
  - "i 0" / "i 1": ignore, the bit afterwards is i.i.d. uniform
  - "r b": read; the model is expected to output the memory bit b.

The probability of "write", "read", "ignore" is (pw, pr, pi). After each
instruction the second-position symbol (0 or 1) is determined: for `w`
and `i` it is i.i.d. uniform; for `r` it MUST be the current memory state,
which is what the model is graded on.

We train on FFL(pi=0.8) (dense) and evaluate read-error rates on
FFL(pi=0.5) (dense in-distribution-ish), FFL(pi=0.98) (sparse tail; long
stretches of ignore) and a long-context variant at T=1024.

The agent only chooses the *architecture* of the autoregressive sequence
model that maps token-id sequences to per-position logits. Optimizer,
data, training loop, and evaluation are FIXED.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import random
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, replace
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Vocabulary
# =====================================================================
# Token-id encoding: a single integer per timestep (instruction-value pair).
# We use the same ordering as the original paper's open implementation:
# 0 = w0, 1 = w1, 2 = i0, 3 = i1, 4 = r0, 5 = r1.
VOCAB_SIZE = 6
TOK_W0, TOK_W1, TOK_I0, TOK_I1, TOK_R0, TOK_R1 = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
WRITE_TOKS = (TOK_W0, TOK_W1)
IGNORE_TOKS = (TOK_I0, TOK_I1)
READ_TOKS = (TOK_R0, TOK_R1)


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Benchmark configuration
# =====================================================================
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskConfig:
    train_len: int = 512
    train_pi: float = 0.8  # p_ignore for the training distribution
    eval_len: int = 512    # evaluation length for the dense/sparse splits
    eval_pi_dense: float = 0.5
    eval_pi_sparse: float = 0.98
    eval_long_pi: float = 0.8
    eval_long_len: int = 1024
    # Optimization
    batch_size: int = 16
    max_steps: int = 3_000
    lr: float = 3e-4
    weight_decay: float = 0.1
    warmup_steps: int = 50
    grad_clip: float = 1.0
    # Data
    train_examples_per_epoch: int = 64_000   # online-ish sampling: 4000 steps * 16 batch
    eval_num_sequences: int = 2_000
    eval_long_num_sequences: int = 500
    # Logging
    log_interval: int = 1000


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EvalReport:
    pi: float
    seq_len: int
    num_sequences: int
    num_reads: int
    num_errors: int
    seq_with_error: int

    @property
    def read_error_rate(self) -> float:
        if self.num_reads == 0:
            return 0.0
        return self.num_errors / self.num_reads

    @property
    def seq_error_rate(self) -> float:
        if self.num_sequences == 0:
            return 0.0
        return self.seq_with_error / self.num_sequences


DEFAULT_TASK = TaskConfig()


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Data generation
# =====================================================================
def set_global_seed(seed: int) -> None:
    random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


def sample_ffl_batch(
    batch_size: int,
    seq_len: int,
    pi: float,
    generator: torch.Generator,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Return a [batch_size, seq_len] tensor of token-ids drawn from FFL.

    The first token is always a write to ensure the memory bit is defined.
    The (pw, pr, pi) triple has pi as given and pw = pr = (1 - pi) / 2.
    """
    pw = pr = (1.0 - pi) / 2.0
    # Sample instruction categories: 0=write, 1=ignore, 2=read.
    probs = torch.tensor([pw, pi, pr], dtype=torch.float32)
    instr = torch.multinomial(
        probs.expand(batch_size * seq_len, -1),
        num_samples=1,
        generator=generator,
    ).view(batch_size, seq_len)
    instr[:, 0] = 0  # first instruction is always a write
    # Sample bit per step (for w/i, this is the visible/random bit; for r,
    # we will overwrite below using the memory state).
    bits = torch.randint(0, 2, (batch_size, seq_len), generator=generator)
    # Walk the memory forward; for read positions, replace bit with memory.
    # Use python loop over seq_len which is small (<= 1024).
    mem = bits[:, 0].clone()  # first token is a write
    out_bits = bits.clone()
    for t in range(1, seq_len):
        is_write = instr[:, t] == 0
        # Memory updates to bits[:, t] where write
        mem = torch.where(is_write, bits[:, t], mem)
        # For reads, the visible bit equals memory
        is_read = instr[:, t] == 2
        out_bits[:, t] = torch.where(is_read, mem, bits[:, t])
    # Map (instruction, bit) -> token id.
    # write -> {TOK_W0, TOK_W1}; ignore -> {TOK_I0, TOK_I1}; read -> {TOK_R0, TOK_R1}.
    instr_offset = instr * 2  # 0, 2, 4
    tokens = instr_offset + out_bits
    return tokens.to(torch.long)


def read_mask(tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Bool mask marking read positions (TOK_R0/TOK_R1)."""
    return (tokens == TOK_R0) | (tokens == TOK_R1)


# =====================================================================
# EDITABLE: build_model
# =====================================================================
# The model is an autoregressive next-token predictor over VOCAB_SIZE tokens.
# Input:  LongTensor [batch, seq_len] of token ids.
# Output: FloatTensor [batch, seq_len, VOCAB_SIZE] of logits.
# At read positions t (where the token is TOK_R0 or TOK_R1), the logits at
# position t-1 are graded against the read-bit. (We use teacher forcing,
# so the model predicts token t from tokens [0..t-1]; the read-position
# probe asks for the next bit at the position *preceding* the read token.)
#
# Implement this as a plain torch.nn.Module. The FIXED training loop uses
# next-token cross-entropy on every position; OOD evaluation only grades
# read positions.
#
# You can choose any architecture (Transformer, attention-regularised
# Transformer, LSTM, S4/SSM, Mamba-style selective recurrence, etc.) as
# long as:
#   - It returns a tensor of shape [batch, seq_len, VOCAB_SIZE].
#   - It is causal (position t depends only on positions <= t).
#   - It runs within the 30-minute single-H100 budget across all 3 evals.
# Total trainable parameters should stay below 50M for memory reasons.
#
# Reference (must-read) paper:
#   Liu, Ash, Goel, Krishnamurthy, Zhang, 2023.
#   "Exposing Attention Glitches with Flip-Flop Language Modeling."
#   arXiv:2306.00946  (R2 shows a 1-layer LSTM is a perfect skyline.)
# =====================================================================
class FlipFlopModel(nn.Module):
    """Default scaffold: a tiny causal Transformer (vanilla, no tricks).

    This default is intentionally weak: it matches the "baseline Transformer"
    described in the paper and so exhibits attention glitches on the sparse
    tail. Replace this class to study an alternative architecture or
    regularisation strategy (see baselines).
    """

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = VOCAB_SIZE, max_len: int = 1024):
        super().__init__()
        d_model = 128
        n_layers = 2
        n_heads = 4
        self.tok = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.pos = nn.Embedding(max_len, d_model)
        self.max_len = max_len
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=d_model,
            nhead=n_heads,
            dim_feedforward=4 * d_model,
            dropout=0.0,
            batch_first=True,
            activation="gelu",
            norm_first=True,
        )
        self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=n_layers)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size, bias=False)

    def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        bsz, seq_len = tokens.shape
        if seq_len > self.max_len:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Sequence length {seq_len} exceeds model max_len {self.max_len}."
            )
        pos_ids = torch.arange(seq_len, device=tokens.device).unsqueeze(0)
        h = self.tok(tokens) + self.pos(pos_ids)
        causal = torch.triu(
            torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len, device=tokens.device, dtype=torch.bool),
            diagonal=1,
        )
        h = self.encoder(h, mask=causal, is_causal=True)
        h = self.norm(h)
        return self.head(h)


def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Construct the autoregressive model graded by the FFLM evaluator."""
    return FlipFlopModel(vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE, max_len=max(config.train_len, config.eval_long_len))


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: training loop and evaluation
# =====================================================================
def _causal_lr_lambda(step: int, warmup: int, total: int) -> float:
    if step < warmup:
        return float(step + 1) / float(max(1, warmup))
    remaining = max(0, total - step)
    return remaining / float(max(1, total - warmup))


def train_model(
    model: nn.Module,
    config: TaskConfig,
    device: torch.device,
    train_seed: int,
) -> None:
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        model.parameters(),
        lr=config.lr,
        betas=(0.9, 0.999),
        weight_decay=config.weight_decay,
    )
    scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LambdaLR(
        optimizer,
        lr_lambda=lambda step: _causal_lr_lambda(
            step, config.warmup_steps, config.max_steps
        ),
    )
    data_generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(train_seed)
    model.train()
    running_loss = 0.0
    running_acc = 0.0
    running_count = 0
    t0 = time.time()
    for step in range(1, config.max_steps + 1):
        tokens = sample_ffl_batch(
            batch_size=config.batch_size,
            seq_len=config.train_len,
            pi=config.train_pi,
            generator=data_generator,
        ).to(device)
        # Teacher-forced next-token prediction
        inp = tokens[:, :-1]
        tgt = tokens[:, 1:]
        logits = model(inp)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(
            logits.reshape(-1, VOCAB_SIZE),
            tgt.reshape(-1),
        )
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss.backward()
        if config.grad_clip > 0:
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), config.grad_clip)
        optimizer.step()
        scheduler.step()

        with torch.no_grad():
            # Read-bit accuracy: restrict argmax to {r0, r1} at read positions,
            # then compare to the target bit (paper-canonical FFLM metric).
            read_logits = logits[..., [TOK_R0, TOK_R1]]
            read_preds = read_logits.argmax(dim=-1)
            target_bits = (tgt == TOK_R1).long()
            mask = read_mask(tgt)
            if mask.any():
                read_correct = ((read_preds == target_bits) & mask).sum().item()
                read_total = mask.sum().item()
            else:
                read_correct = 0
                read_total = 0
            running_loss += float(loss.item())
            running_acc += read_correct
            running_count += read_total
        if step == 1 or step % config.log_interval == 0 or step == config.max_steps:
            denom = max(1, running_count)
            avg_loss = running_loss / max(1, min(step, config.log_interval))
            avg_acc = running_acc / denom if denom > 0 else 0.0
            elapsed = time.time() - t0
            print(
                "TRAIN_METRICS "
                f"step={step} loss={avg_loss:.6f} read_acc={avg_acc:.6f} "
                f"reads_in_window={running_count} elapsed_s={elapsed:.1f}",
                flush=True,
            )
            running_loss = 0.0
            running_acc = 0.0
            running_count = 0


@torch.no_grad()
def evaluate_split(
    model: nn.Module,
    pi: float,
    seq_len: int,
    num_sequences: int,
    device: torch.device,
    eval_seed: int,
    eval_batch: int = 64,
) -> EvalReport:
    """Grade read-bit predictions per Liu et al. (NeurIPS 2023).

    At every read position t (where tokens[:, t] is TOK_R0 or TOK_R1),
    we ask: conditional on the next token being a read, did the model
    assign higher probability to the correct bit? This restricts the
    softmax to the two read tokens (r0 vs r1) and compares to the
    target bit. This is the standard FFLM evaluation: it isolates the
    memory-recall question from the (unrelated, unpredictable) question
    of whether the next instruction will be write/ignore/read.
    """
    model.eval()
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(eval_seed)
    num_errors = 0
    num_reads = 0
    seq_with_error = 0
    total_seq = 0
    remaining = num_sequences
    while remaining > 0:
        b = min(eval_batch, remaining)
        tokens = sample_ffl_batch(
            batch_size=b,
            seq_len=seq_len,
            pi=pi,
            generator=generator,
        ).to(device)
        inp = tokens[:, :-1]
        tgt = tokens[:, 1:]
        logits = model(inp)
        # Restrict comparison to the two read-token logits.
        read_logits = logits[..., [TOK_R0, TOK_R1]]   # [bsz, seq-1, 2]
        read_preds = read_logits.argmax(dim=-1)        # 0 -> r0, 1 -> r1
        # Target read-bit: 0 if target is TOK_R0, 1 if target is TOK_R1.
        target_bits = (tgt == TOK_R1).long()
        mask = read_mask(tgt)
        errors = mask & (read_preds != target_bits)
        num_errors += int(errors.sum().item())
        num_reads += int(mask.sum().item())
        per_seq_errors = errors.sum(dim=1)
        seq_with_error += int((per_seq_errors > 0).sum().item())
        total_seq += b
        remaining -= b
    return EvalReport(
        pi=pi,
        seq_len=seq_len,
        num_sequences=total_seq,
        num_reads=num_reads,
        num_errors=num_errors,
        seq_with_error=seq_with_error,
    )


def resolve_device(device_arg: str) -> torch.device:
    if device_arg == "cpu":
        return torch.device("cpu")
    if device_arg == "cuda":
        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
            raise RuntimeError("CUDA requested but no GPU is available.")
        return torch.device("cuda")
    return torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")


def run_benchmark(
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
    device: torch.device,
    eval_pi: float,
    eval_len: int,
    eval_num_sequences: int,
    eval_batch: int,
    label: str,
) -> dict:
    set_global_seed(seed)
    print(
        "TASK_CONFIG "
        f"label={label} train_len={config.train_len} train_pi={config.train_pi} "
        f"eval_len={eval_len} eval_pi={eval_pi} max_steps={config.max_steps} "
        f"batch_size={config.batch_size} eval_batch={eval_batch} "
        f"lr={config.lr} wd={config.weight_decay}",
        flush=True,
    )
    model = build_model(config).to(device)
    n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
    print(f"MODEL_INFO num_params={n_params}", flush=True)

    train_model(model, config, device, train_seed=seed * 9973 + 1)

    report = evaluate_split(
        model=model,
        pi=eval_pi,
        seq_len=eval_len,
        num_sequences=eval_num_sequences,
        device=device,
        eval_seed=seed * 7919 + 11,
        eval_batch=eval_batch,
    )
    # Lower error rate is better; we expose a [0, 1] "score" computed as
    # 1 - sequence_error_rate so higher is better.
    score = max(0.0, 1.0 - report.seq_error_rate)
    metrics = {
        "read_error_rate": report.read_error_rate,
        "seq_error_rate": report.seq_error_rate,
        "score": score,
        "num_reads": float(report.num_reads),
        "num_sequences": float(report.num_sequences),
        "seq_with_error": float(report.seq_with_error),
        "num_params": float(n_params),
    }
    print(
        "FINAL_METRICS "
        + " ".join(
            f"{key}={value:.6f}" if isinstance(value, float) else f"{key}={value}"
            for key, value in metrics.items()
        ),
        flush=True,
    )
    # TEST_METRICS is the framework-canonical line.
    print(
        f"TEST_METRICS read_error_rate={metrics['read_error_rate']:.8f} "
        f"seq_error_rate={metrics['seq_error_rate']:.8f} score={metrics['score']:.6f}",
        flush=True,
    )
    return metrics


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run the synth-flip-flop task.")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--label", type=str, default="dense")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--device",
        choices=("auto", "cpu", "cuda"),
        default="auto",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--split",
        choices=("dense", "sparse", "long_ctx"),
        default="dense",
        help="Which OOD evaluation split to grade against.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=None)
    return parser.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    config = DEFAULT_TASK
    if args.max_steps is not None:
        config = replace(config, max_steps=args.max_steps)
    if args.batch_size is not None:
        config = replace(config, batch_size=args.batch_size)

    if args.split == "dense":
        eval_pi = config.eval_pi_dense
        eval_len = config.eval_len
        eval_num = config.eval_num_sequences
        eval_batch = 64
    elif args.split == "sparse":
        eval_pi = config.eval_pi_sparse
        eval_len = config.eval_len
        eval_num = config.eval_num_sequences
        eval_batch = 64
    else:  # long_ctx
        eval_pi = config.eval_long_pi
        eval_len = config.eval_long_len
        eval_num = config.eval_long_num_sequences
        # Long-context Transformer attention has a much larger activation
        # footprint. The three task splits run concurrently in one baseline
        # invocation, so keep this batch small enough to finish reliably.
        eval_batch = 8

    device = resolve_device(args.device)
    metrics = run_benchmark(
        config=config,
        seed=args.seed,
        device=device,
        eval_pi=eval_pi,
        eval_len=eval_len,
        eval_num_sequences=eval_num,
        eval_batch=eval_batch,
        label=args.label,
    )

    if args.output_dir is not None:
        args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        output_path = args.output_dir / f"{args.label}_seed{args.seed}.json"
        output_path.write_text(json.dumps({"config": asdict(config), "metrics": metrics}, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

class FlipFlopModel(nn.Module):
    """Vanilla causal Transformer (the 'baseline' from the paper)."""

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = VOCAB_SIZE, max_len: int = 1024):
        super().__init__()
        d_model = 256
        n_layers = 4
        n_heads = 8
        self.tok = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.pos = nn.Embedding(max_len, d_model)
        self.max_len = max_len
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=d_model,
            nhead=n_heads,
            dim_feedforward=4 * d_model,
            dropout=0.0,
            batch_first=True,
            activation="gelu",
            norm_first=True,
        )
        self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=n_layers)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size, bias=False)

    def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        bsz, seq_len = tokens.shape
        if seq_len > self.max_len:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Sequence length {seq_len} exceeds model max_len {self.max_len}."
            )
        pos_ids = torch.arange(seq_len, device=tokens.device).unsqueeze(0)
        h = self.tok(tokens) + self.pos(pos_ids)
        causal = torch.triu(
            torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len, device=tokens.device, dtype=torch.bool),
            diagonal=1,
        )
        h = self.encoder(h, mask=causal, is_causal=True)
        h = self.norm(h)
        return self.head(h)


def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Construct the vanilla-Transformer FFLM."""
    return FlipFlopModel(
        vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE,
        max_len=max(config.train_len, config.eval_long_len),
    )

class _SharpCausalAttention(nn.Module):
    """Multi-head causal self-attention with a sharpening temperature.

    The sharpening temperature divides the attention logits before the
    softmax, producing peaked (near-hard) attention. This matches the
    behaviour the paper documents for the entropy-regularised models.
    """

    def __init__(self, d_model: int, n_heads: int, temperature: float = 0.5):
        super().__init__()
        assert d_model % n_heads == 0
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.head_dim = d_model // n_heads
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(d_model, 3 * d_model, bias=True)
        self.proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model, bias=True)
        self.temperature = temperature

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        bsz, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        qkv = self.qkv(x).reshape(bsz, seq_len, 3, self.n_heads, self.head_dim)
        q, k, v = qkv.unbind(dim=2)
        q = q.transpose(1, 2)
        k = k.transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.transpose(1, 2)
        scale = 1.0 / (math.sqrt(self.head_dim) * self.temperature)
        scores = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) * scale
        causal = torch.triu(
            torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len, device=x.device, dtype=torch.bool),
            diagonal=1,
        )
        scores = scores.masked_fill(causal, float("-inf"))
        attn = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        out = torch.matmul(attn, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(bsz, seq_len, self.d_model)
        return self.proj(out)


class _SharpBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, n_heads: int, temperature: float = 0.5):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.attn = _SharpCausalAttention(d_model, n_heads, temperature=temperature)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(d_model, 4 * d_model),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(4 * d_model, d_model),
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = x + self.attn(self.norm1(x))
        x = x + self.mlp(self.norm2(x))
        return x


class FlipFlopModel(nn.Module):
    """Attention-sharpened causal Transformer for FFLM."""

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = VOCAB_SIZE, max_len: int = 1024):
        super().__init__()
        d_model = 256
        n_layers = 4
        n_heads = 8
        self.tok = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.pos = nn.Embedding(max_len, d_model)
        self.max_len = max_len
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
            [_SharpBlock(d_model, n_heads, temperature=0.5) for _ in range(n_layers)]
        )
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size, bias=False)

    def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        bsz, seq_len = tokens.shape
        if seq_len > self.max_len:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Sequence length {seq_len} exceeds model max_len {self.max_len}."
            )
        pos_ids = torch.arange(seq_len, device=tokens.device).unsqueeze(0)
        h = self.tok(tokens) + self.pos(pos_ids)
        for block in self.blocks:
            h = block(h)
        h = self.norm(h)
        return self.head(h)


def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Construct the attention-sharpened Transformer FFLM."""
    return FlipFlopModel(
        vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE,
        max_len=max(config.train_len, config.eval_long_len),
    )

class _SelectiveSSMBlock(nn.Module):
    """A single Mamba-style selective diagonal-SSM block.

    Input/output shape: [batch, seq_len, d_model].
    Internally we project to a small d_state=8 width and use a python
    loop to apply the data-dependent recurrence (no CUDA kernel).
    """

    def __init__(self, d_model: int, d_state: int = 8, expand: int = 2):
        super().__init__()
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.d_state = d_state
        self.d_inner = d_model * expand
        self.in_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, 2 * self.d_inner, bias=False)
        self.conv1d = nn.Conv1d(
            self.d_inner, self.d_inner,
            kernel_size=3, padding=2, groups=self.d_inner, bias=True,
        )
        # x_proj produces (delta, B, C) per timestep.
        self.x_proj = nn.Linear(self.d_inner, d_state * 2 + 1, bias=False)
        self.dt_proj = nn.Linear(1, self.d_inner, bias=True)
        # Learnable per-channel state-decay matrix (log A_d).
        A = torch.arange(1, d_state + 1, dtype=torch.float32).repeat(self.d_inner, 1)
        self.A_log = nn.Parameter(torch.log(A))  # [d_inner, d_state]
        self.D = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(self.d_inner))
        self.out_proj = nn.Linear(self.d_inner, d_model, bias=False)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)

    def _selective_scan(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        delta: torch.Tensor,
        A: torch.Tensor,
        B: torch.Tensor,
        C: torch.Tensor,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        # x:     [bsz, seq, d_inner]
        # delta: [bsz, seq, d_inner]   (positive)
        # A:     [d_inner, d_state]    (negative; we apply exp(delta*A))
        # B,C:   [bsz, seq, d_state]
        bsz, seq_len, d_inner = x.shape
        d_state = A.shape[1]
        # deltaA: [bsz, seq, d_inner, d_state] = exp(-delta * A)
        deltaA = torch.exp(-(delta.unsqueeze(-1) * A))
        # deltaB_u: [bsz, seq, d_inner, d_state] = delta * B * x
        deltaB_u = delta.unsqueeze(-1) * B.unsqueeze(2) * x.unsqueeze(-1)
        h = torch.zeros(bsz, d_inner, d_state, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        ys = []
        # The only sequential loop is over time; d_state is capped at 8 in
        # this baseline so each step remains a small batched tensor update.
        for t in range(seq_len):
            h = deltaA[:, t] * h + deltaB_u[:, t]
            # y_t = sum_state h * C_t   -> [bsz, d_inner]
            y_t = (h * C[:, t].unsqueeze(1)).sum(dim=-1)
            ys.append(y_t)
        return torch.stack(ys, dim=1)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        residual = x
        x = self.norm(x)
        bsz, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        xz = self.in_proj(x)               # [bsz, seq, 2*d_inner]
        x_in, z = xz.chunk(2, dim=-1)      # each [bsz, seq, d_inner]
        # Causal depthwise conv along time (right-truncate by kernel-1).
        x_conv = self.conv1d(x_in.transpose(1, 2))[..., :seq_len]
        x_conv = F.silu(x_conv.transpose(1, 2))
        proj = self.x_proj(x_conv)
        delta_raw, B, C = torch.split(
            proj, [1, self.d_state, self.d_state], dim=-1,
        )
        delta = F.softplus(self.dt_proj(delta_raw))  # [bsz, seq, d_inner]
        A = torch.exp(self.A_log)                    # [d_inner, d_state]
        y = self._selective_scan(x_conv, delta, A, B, C)
        y = y + x_conv * self.D
        y = y * F.silu(z)
        return residual + self.out_proj(y)


class FlipFlopModel(nn.Module):
    """Mamba-style selective SSM stack.

    We keep the model deliberately small (d_model=64, d_state=8, 1 block)
    so the python-level scan stays inside the per-baseline 30-min budget.
    A 1-bit memory is trivially representable so further width is
    unnecessary.
    """

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = VOCAB_SIZE, max_len: int = 1024):
        super().__init__()
        d_model = 64
        n_layers = 1
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
            [_SelectiveSSMBlock(d_model=d_model, d_state=8, expand=2)
             for _ in range(n_layers)]
        )
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size, bias=False)
        self.max_len = max_len

    def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        h = self.embed(tokens)
        for block in self.blocks:
            h = block(h)
        h = self.norm(h)
        return self.head(h)


def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Construct the simplified-Mamba FFLM."""
    return FlipFlopModel(
        vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE,
        max_len=max(config.train_len, config.eval_long_len),
    )

tasks.name: Deep Matrix Factorization Recovery
tasks.summary: Studies how matrix-factorization parameterizations and optimizers recover low-rank matrices from sparse observations.
tasks.description_md:
# Synthetic Matrix Completion: Neural Matrix Factorization Architecture

## Research Question
Given a sparse subset of entries of an unknown rank-r ground-truth matrix M*,
how should we **parameterize a neural matrix factorization** (depth, initialization,
regularization, optimizer) so that gradient descent recovers M* as accurately
as possible on the *unobserved* entries?

This is the canonical "deep matrix factorization" question studied by Arora,
Cohen, Hu, Luo, "Implicit Regularization in Deep Matrix Factorization"
(NeurIPS 2019; [arXiv:1905.13655](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.13655)). They
showed empirically that *increasing the depth* of the factorization
M = W_d W_{d-1} ... W_1 introduces a stronger implicit bias toward low-rank
solutions, often beating both shallow factorizations and classical
nuclear-norm minimization.

## Background
Low-rank matrix completion is fundamental in collaborative filtering, signal
processing, and statistics. Classical approaches solve a convex relaxation
(minimize nuclear norm subject to fitting the observations) via algorithms
like SVT ([Cai-Candes-Shen 2010](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.3286)) or perform
explicit non-convex factorization via alternating minimization
([Jain-Netrapalli-Sanghavi 2012](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.0467)).

Deep matrix factorization replaces the explicit rank constraint with depth:
write M as a product of d square (full hidden dim) bias-free linear layers
and minimize the squared error on observed entries by gradient descent. With
small initialization the resulting solution biases towards low effective
rank, and depth d >= 3 makes this bias sharper than depth 2 (and stronger
than the implicit nuclear-norm regularizer at low observation rates).

## What You Can Modify
Edit the scaffold file `pytorch-examples/synth_matrix_completion/custom_strategy.py`
inside the EDITABLE block. Concretely, the editable region contains:

1. `build_strategy() -> MatrixRecoveryStrategy` — the entry point the driver calls.
2. The `MatrixRecoveryStrategy` interface declaration.
3. One or more reference strategy classes (default: `DeepMatrixFactorization`).

You may completely replace the strategy class with any algorithm you like
(deeper factorizations, alternative initializations, balanced
parameterization, IRLS, ADMM, SVT, AltMin, neural ODE inits, etc.) as long
as the returned object implements `recover(observed_values, observed_mask,
n, rank_hint, device, max_iters, log_iters) -> torch.Tensor` of shape
`[n, n]`.

## Fixed Setup
- **Ground truth**: random rank-r matrix M* = (U V^T) / sqrt(r) with
  U, V ~ N(0, 1) i.i.d. of shape `[n, r]`, rescaled to `||M*||_F = n`.
  (Same construction as Arora et al. 2019; `gen_gt.py` in their repo.)
- **Observations**: uniformly random subset of the n*n entries at the
  configured observation rate (`gen_obs.py` in the reference repo).
- **Driver**: in the release configuration, samples one matrix and runs
  one initialization per top-level seed, then calls `strategy.recover(...)`
  with a hard iteration budget.
- **Metric**: relative Frobenius error on the *unobserved* entries
  (`test_rel_fro = ||(estimate - M*)[~mask]||_F / ||M*[~mask]||_F`), where
  lower is better. A derived `score = max(0, 1 - test_rel_fro)` may be printed
  for feedback, but the benchmark score spec uses `test_rel_fro` directly.
- Compute budget: each test command must finish in under 30 minutes on a
  single H100.

## Interface Notes
- `recover(...)` receives `observed_values` (M* masked to zero off the
  observation set), `observed_mask` (bool [n, n]), `n`, `rank_hint`
  (the true rank — you may use or ignore), `device`, `max_iters`, and
  `log_iters`.
- Return a CPU or GPU `torch.Tensor` of shape `[n, n]`. The driver moves
  it to CPU and casts to float32.
- Please emit `TRAIN_METRICS iter=... train_mse=...` periodically so the
  agent loop sees training progress.

## Fixed Setup
Three configurations are evaluated:
- `rank3-50`: n=50, rank=3, 30% observed.
- `rank5-100`: n=100, rank=5, 20% observed (the canonical Arora setup).
- `rank10-200`: n=200, rank=10, 10% observed (harder, larger-scale).

The leaderboard primary metric per environment is `test_rel_fro` (lower better).
The task-level score is the geometric mean of normalized `test_rel_fro` terms
across the three environments.

## Baselines
- **shallow_mf** — Depth-2 matrix factorization (`M = W_2 W_1`),
  Gaussian init scale `1e-3`, Adam. Mirrors the depth-2 curve of Arora
  et al. (2019), Figure 1.
- **nuclear_norm** — Singular Value Thresholding ([SVT, Cai-Candes-Shen
  2010, arXiv:0810.3286](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.3286)) with `tau = 5n`
  and step size `delta = 1.2 / observation_rate`. Classical convex
  baseline.
- **deep_mf** — Depth-3 deep matrix factorization with small Gaussian
  init (`init_scale = 1e-3`) and learning rate `1e-3`, Adam. The depth-3
  setup of Arora et al. (2019), Figure 1.

Synthetic Matrix Completion: Neural Matrix Factorization Architecture

Research Question

Given a sparse subset of entries of an unknown rank-r ground-truth matrix M, how should we parameterize a neural matrix factorization (depth, initialization, regularization, optimizer) so that gradient descent recovers M as accurately as possible on the unobserved entries?

This is the canonical "deep matrix factorization" question studied by Arora, Cohen, Hu, Luo, "Implicit Regularization in Deep Matrix Factorization" (NeurIPS 2019; arXiv:1905.13655). They showed empirically that increasing the depth of the factorization M = W_d W_{d-1} ... W_1 introduces a stronger implicit bias toward low-rank solutions, often beating both shallow factorizations and classical nuclear-norm minimization.

Background

Low-rank matrix completion is fundamental in collaborative filtering, signal processing, and statistics. Classical approaches solve a convex relaxation (minimize nuclear norm subject to fitting the observations) via algorithms like SVT (Cai-Candes-Shen 2010) or perform explicit non-convex factorization via alternating minimization (Jain-Netrapalli-Sanghavi 2012).

Deep matrix factorization replaces the explicit rank constraint with depth: write M as a product of d square (full hidden dim) bias-free linear layers and minimize the squared error on observed entries by gradient descent. With small initialization the resulting solution biases towards low effective rank, and depth d >= 3 makes this bias sharper than depth 2 (and stronger than the implicit nuclear-norm regularizer at low observation rates).

What You Can Modify

Edit the scaffold file pytorch-examples/synth_matrix_completion/custom_strategy.py inside the EDITABLE block. Concretely, the editable region contains:

  1. build_strategy() -> MatrixRecoveryStrategy — the entry point the driver calls.
  2. The MatrixRecoveryStrategy interface declaration.
  3. One or more reference strategy classes (default: DeepMatrixFactorization).

You may completely replace the strategy class with any algorithm you like (deeper factorizations, alternative initializations, balanced parameterization, IRLS, ADMM, SVT, AltMin, neural ODE inits, etc.) as long as the returned object implements recover(observed_values, observed_mask, n, rank_hint, device, max_iters, log_iters) -> torch.Tensor of shape [n, n].

Fixed Setup

  • Ground truth: random rank-r matrix M* = (U V^T) / sqrt(r) with U, V ~ N(0, 1) i.i.d. of shape [n, r], rescaled to ||M*||_F = n. (Same construction as Arora et al. 2019; gen_gt.py in their repo.)
  • Observations: uniformly random subset of the n*n entries at the configured observation rate (gen_obs.py in the reference repo).
  • Driver: in the release configuration, samples one matrix and runs one initialization per top-level seed, then calls strategy.recover(...) with a hard iteration budget.
  • Metric: relative Frobenius error on the unobserved entries (test_rel_fro = ||(estimate - M*)[~mask]||_F / ||M*[~mask]||_F), where lower is better. A derived score = max(0, 1 - test_rel_fro) may be printed for feedback, but the benchmark score spec uses test_rel_fro directly.
  • Compute budget: each test command must finish in under 30 minutes on a single H100.

Interface Notes

  • recover(...) receives observed_values (M* masked to zero off the observation set), observed_mask (bool [n, n]), n, rank_hint (the true rank — you may use or ignore), device, max_iters, and log_iters.
  • Return a CPU or GPU torch.Tensor of shape [n, n]. The driver moves it to CPU and casts to float32.
  • Please emit TRAIN_METRICS iter=... train_mse=... periodically so the agent loop sees training progress.

Fixed Setup

Three configurations are evaluated: - rank3-50: n=50, rank=3, 30% observed. - rank5-100: n=100, rank=5, 20% observed (the canonical Arora setup). - rank10-200: n=200, rank=10, 10% observed (harder, larger-scale).

The leaderboard primary metric per environment is test_rel_fro (lower better). The task-level score is the geometric mean of normalized test_rel_fro terms across the three environments.

Baselines

  • shallow_mf — Depth-2 matrix factorization (M = W_2 W_1), Gaussian init scale 1e-3, Adam. Mirrors the depth-2 curve of Arora et al. (2019), Figure 1.
  • nuclear_norm — Singular Value Thresholding (SVT, Cai-Candes-Shen 2010, arXiv:0810.3286) with tau = 5n and step size delta = 1.2 / observation_rate. Classical convex baseline.
  • deep_mf — Depth-3 deep matrix factorization with small Gaussian init (init_scale = 1e-3) and learning rate 1e-3, Adam. The depth-3 setup of Arora et al. (2019), Figure 1.
